entries.title: FKNMS: sanctuary-wide prohibitions
entries.effect: Sanctuary-wide: no coral contact/take, no explosives, marine-life harvest only per FAC 68B-42. NOT a spearfishing ban by itself.
entries.excerpt: Harvesting, possessing, or landing any marine life species, or part thereof, within the Sanctuary, except in accordance with rules 68B-42 of the Florida Administrative Code, and such rules shall apply mutatis mutandis (with necessary editorial changes) to all Federal and State waters within the Sanctuary.
entries.note: The sanctuary-wide rule does not close the Keys to spearfishing. The closures are area-specific — see § 922.164. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: FKNMS: Key Largo & Looe Key Existing Management Areas
entries.effect: Carrying or possessing a speargun, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or sling is itself an offence unless in uninterrupted transit.
entries.excerpt: Fishing with, carrying or possessing, except while passing through without interruption or for law enforcement purposes: pole spears, air rifles, bows and arrows, slings, Hawaiian slings, rubber powered arbaletes, pneumatic and spring-loaded guns or similar devices known as spearguns.
entries.scope: Key Largo Management Area and Looe Key Management Area (boundaries at 15 C.F.R. pt. 922 subpt. P, app. II).
entries.note: The strictest gear-possession rule anywhere in Florida. Stow the gun and keep moving. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: FKNMS: Sanctuary Preservation Areas & Ecological Reserves
entries.effect: All 18 SPAs and both Ecological Reserves are absolute no-fishing zones. Spearfishing included.
entries.excerpt: Except for catch and release fishing by trolling in the Conch Reef, Alligator Reef, Sombrero Reef, and Sand Key SPAs, fishing by any means.
entries.scope: 18 SPAs (app. V): Alligator Reef, Carysfort/South Carysfort, Cheeca Rocks, Coffins Patch, Conch Reef, Davis Reef, Dry Rocks, Grecian Rocks, Eastern Dry Rocks, The Elbow, French Reef, Hen and Chickens, Looe Key, Molasses Reef, Newfound Harbor Key, Rock Key, Sand Key, Sombrero Key. Ecological Reserves (app. IV): Western Sambo; Tortugas North and South.
entries.note: THE KEYS ARE UNDER TWO DIFFERENT RULEBOOKS AT ONCE. The 2025 Restoration Blueprint took effect in FEDERAL sanctuary waters on 5 March 2025. Florida's Governor certified it unacceptable under NMSA § 304(b), so FLORIDA STATE WATERS remain on the 1997 zoning. On the federal side the catch-and-release trolling exception at Conch, Alligator, Sombrero and Sand Key is GONE. Compounding this, eCFR's ‘current’ text of §§ 922.163 and 922.164 still renders the pre-2025 scheme — the § 922.164 source credit stops at 74 FR 38095 (31 July 2009) — so anyone reading eCFR is reading state-waters law only. This map's Keys layer is built from NOAA's own post-Blueprint GIS and every zone carries a state/federal flag. Confirm with FKNMS (305-809-4700) before relying on it. entries.title: South Atlantic deepwater MPAs
entries.effect: No fishing for or possession of South Atlantic snapper-grouper. Transit allowed with gear stowed.
entries.excerpt: No person may fish for a South Atlantic snapper-grouper in an MPA, and no person may possess a South Atlantic snapper-grouper in an MPA.
entries.full: No person may fish for a South Atlantic snapper-grouper in an MPA, and no person may possess a South Atlantic snapper-grouper in an MPA. However, the prohibition on possession does not apply to a person aboard a vessel that is in transit with fishing gear appropriately stowed as specified in paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section. In addition to these restrictions, see § 635.21(d)(1)(iii) of this chapter regarding restrictions applicable within these MPAs for any vessel issued a permit under part 635 of this chapter that has longline gear on board.
entries.scope: Eight MPAs; three lie off Florida: North Florida MPA, St. Lucie Hump MPA, East Hump MPA. Coordinates at § 622.183(a)(1)(i)(A) to (H).

entries.title: Dry Tortugas National Park
entries.effect: Spearfishing expressly prohibited by every gear name. Hook-and-line only.

entries.title: Spearfishing: statutory closures
entries.effect: Closes John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, the waters of Collier County, and the Upper Keys. Possession of a spear in the water there is prima facie evidence of a violation.
entries.excerpt: Except as otherwise provided by commission rule or order, spearfishing is prohibited within the boundaries of the John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, the waters of Collier County, and the area in Monroe County known as Upper Keys, which includes all salt waters under the jurisdiction of the commission beginning at the county line between Miami-Dade and Monroe Counties and running south, including all of the keys down to and including Long Key.
entries.full:
(1) For the purposes of this section, 'spearfishing' means the taking of any saltwater fish through the instrumentality of a spear, gig, or lance operated by a person swimming at or below the surface of the water.

(2)(b) ... the possession in the water of a spear, gig, or lance by a person swimming at or below the surface of the water in a prohibited area is prima facie evidence of a violation ...

(3) The commission may create additional restricted areas following investigation, application by local governing bodies, publication in local newspapers, and a local agreement to post and maintain notices.

(4) A person who violates this section commits a Level Two violation under s. 379.401.
entries.note: IMPORTANT: FWC has REOPENED Collier County by rule — see 68B-20.003(1)(a). The statute's Collier closure is superseded. The Monroe/Upper Keys closure stands: Miami-Dade county line south through and including Long Key. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Definitions: spearing, spearfishing, gigging, bow hunting
entries.effect: Gigging (at or above the surface) and spearfishing (in the water) are legally distinct categories.
entries.excerpt: 'Gigging' means the catching or taking of a fish through the instrumentality of a single or multi-pronged gig or spear, barbed or barbless, deployed at or above the surface of the water. 'Spearfishing' means the catching or taking of a fish through the instrumentality of a hand or mechanically propelled, single or multi-pronged spear or lance [operated by a person in the water]. 'Spearing' means the catching or taking of a fish by bow hunting, gigging, spearfishing, or by any device used to capture a fish by piercing its body [excluding hook-and-line and snagging].
entries.note: This distinction matters: a rule that says 'spearing' catches gigging too; a rule that says 'spearfishing' does not. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: matched apart from paragraph labels or typography.

entries.title: Statewide spearing rule: closures are the exceptions, and Collier County is restored
entries.effect: In its own words the rule makes spearing "lawful in all salt waters and salt tributaries" of Florida except where § 379.2425 or Division 68B closes it, and it lifts the statutory Collier County closure. Federal rules, local ordinances and posted signs close more water, so this rule alone never shows that a particular place is open.
entries.excerpt: Spearing is lawful in all salt waters and salt tributaries located in the State of Florida except: (a) As provided in Section 379.2425, F.S. Notwithstanding the prohibition contained in that section, spearfishing is allowed in state waters off Collier County except as prohibited in this chapter and elsewhere in Division 68B, F.A.C.; and, (b) As prohibited in this chapter, and elsewhere in Division 68B, F.A.C.
entries.note: This subsection is often missed. Collier County is not closed by statute, because this rule lifts the closure the statute names. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: The four statewide buffers
entries.effect: 100 yd from bathing beaches, fishing piers and fishable bridges; 100 ft from jetties; all state park waters.
entries.excerpt: (2) Except as provided in Rule 68B-20.004, F.A.C., spearfishing is hereby prohibited: (a) Within 100 yards of all public bathing beaches. (b) Within 100 yards of all commercial or public fishing piers. (c) Within 100 yards of that portion of any bridge where public fishing is legally permitted. (d) Within 100 feet of the unsubmerged portion of any jetty, except that spearfishing shall be allowed along the last 500 yards of any jetty that extends more than 1,500 yards from the shoreline. (e) In or on any body of water under the jurisdiction of the Division of Recreation and Parks of the Department of Environmental Protection. Possession of spearing equipment in or on any body of water under the jurisdiction of the Division of Recreation and Parks is prohibited except when such equipment is not loaded and is properly stored upon watercraft passing nonstop through such marine waters.
entries.note: THE JETTY BUFFER IS 100 FEET, NOT 100 YARDS — the other three are 100 yards. That unit change is the single most dangerous thing in this rule. The list ENDS at (e); there is no (f). The chapeau reads 'Except as provided in Rule 68B-20.004, F.A.C., SPEARFISHING is hereby prohibited' — the operative word is spearfishing, not spearing, so gigging deployed at or above the surface is NOT caught by (a)-(d). Only (e) reaches the broader term 'spearing equipment'. Every buffer is feature-relative; FWC publishes no authoritative geometry, so every buffer on this map is digitized and approximate. Buffer (c) attaches only to bridge portions 'where public fishing is legally permitted' — see § 316.1305. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Powerheads, bangsticks, rebreathers, freshwater
entries.effect: No powerheads or bangsticks to harvest. No harvest on a rebreather except lionfish. No spearing marine species in fresh water.
entries.excerpt: No person shall use any powerhead to harvest any fish in state waters. Powerheads may be possessed while diving in state waters for the purpose of personal protection. Except for persons harvesting lionfish (genus Pterois), no person diving in state waters by means of a rebreather shall harvest any marine species.
entries.note: Possession aboard a vessel of any non-lionfish taken by powerhead or rebreather is itself a violation. Also prohibits harvesting marine species with a hand- or mechanically-propelled spear while diving in fresh water. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: matched apart from paragraph labels or typography.

entries.title: Species that may never be taken by spear
entries.effect: 28 species and family groups. Broader than FWC's public digest.
entries.excerpt: The spearing of the following species and species groups is prohibited: (1) Billfish (species of the genus Xiphias, Istiophorus, Makaira, and Tetrapturus). (2) Sturgeon (Acipenser oxyrhynchus). (3) Tarpon (Megalops atlanticus). (4) Bonefish (Albula vulpes). (5) Jewfish (Epinephelus itajara). (6) Nassau grouper (Epinephelus striatus). (7) Permit (Trachinotus falcatus). (8) Pompano (Trachinotus carolinus). (9) African pompano (Alectis ciliaris). (10) Sharks as defined in Rule 68B-44.002, F.A.C. (11) Spotted eagle ray (Aetobatus narinari). (12) Manta ray (species of the genus Manta and Mobula). (13) Snook (species of the genus Centropomus). (14) Red drum (Sciaenops ocellatus). (15) Spotted seatrout (Cynoscion nebulosus). (16) Weakfish (Cynoscion regalis). (17) Tripletail (Lobotes surinamensis). (18) Surgeonfish (family Acanthuridae). (19) Trumpetfish (family Aulostomidae). (20) Angelfish and butterflyfish (family Chaetodontidae). (21) Porcupinefish (family Diodontidae). (22) Cornetfish (family Fistulariidae). (23) Squirrelfish (family Holocentridae). (24) Trunkfish (family Ostraciidae). (25) Damselfish (family Pomacentridae). (26) Parrotfish (family Scaridae). (27) Pipefish and Seahorse (family Sygnathidae). (28) Puffers (family Tetraodontidae).

This rule has not been amended since 1 January 1998 (flrules.org, checked 29 Sep 2026). entries.cite: Palm Beach County Code, App. G, ch. 13, art. II, div. 2, §§ 13-54 to 13-59
entries.title: Palm Beach spearfishing refuge areas (Laws of Fla. ch. 59-1699)
entries.effect: Two latitude-bounded refuges off Palm Beach where spearfishing on underwater breathing apparatus is prohibited. Freediving is NOT restricted by this division.
entries.excerpt: § 13-56: No person may engage in spear fishing within any of the above described refuge areas while using underwater breathing apparatus.
entries.full:
§ 13-55 — Area No. 1 is bounded on the South by Latitude 26° 44' 51" N and on the North by Latitude 26° 45' 48" N. Area No. 2 is bounded on the South by Latitude 26° 46' 38" N and on the North by Latitude 26° 47' 38" N. Excluding however, from the above defined refuge areas those waters of a depth of less than thirty (30) feet at mean low water and those waters lying less than seven hundred fifty (750) yards from the mean high water line of the shoreline of the Atlantic Ocean.

§ 13-54(d) defines 'underwater breathing apparatus' broadly — self-contained or surface-supplied, any gas, any apparatus letting a submerged person breathe without surfacing.

§ 13-57 makes possession of scuba plus a spear inside a refuge prima facie evidence — EXCEPT when in a boat or conveyance used to transport them. Transiting with tanks and a gun aboard is expressly fine. Barbless knives and lances carried purely for protection are carved out.

§ 13-59 makes violation of Division 2 a misdemeanour.
entries.scope: Area No. 1: 26.747500 N to 26.763333 N. Area No. 2: 26.777222 N to 26.793889 N. The 0.83 nm gap between them (26.763333 to 26.777222 N) is unrestricted, and the north jetty tip at 26.773512 N sits inside it.
entries.note: SCUBA ONLY. A breath-hold diver is outside § 13-56's operative prohibition. The 1959 prose landmarks are expressly 'approximate'; the latitudes control. The 750 yd and 30 ft carve-outs rescue no offshore site. Read verbatim from Municode 21 Aug 2026; browser check 30 Sep 2026. Session law ch. 59-1699 (HB 1997, filed 17 Jun 1959) read 7 Oct 2026 from the State Library scan (LOF1959V2Pt3Ch1670-1754.pdf, printed pp. 3244 to 3246): latitudes and carve-outs match § 13-55. entries.title: Divers-down device
entries.effect: Flag or buoy required. 100 ft stay-near in rivers, inlets and navigation channels; 300 ft everywhere else.
entries.excerpt: (1)(a) "Diver" means a person who is wholly or partially submerged in the waters of the state and is equipped with a face mask and snorkel or underwater breathing apparatus. ... (2) All divers must prominently display a divers-down warning device in the area in which the diving occurs, other than when diving in an area customarily used for swimming only. A divers-down buoy may not be used or displayed onboard a vessel. ... (4) Divers shall make reasonable efforts to stay within 100 feet of a divers-down warning device on rivers, inlets, and navigation channels. A person operating a vessel on a river, inlet, or navigation channel must make a reasonable effort to maintain a distance of at least 100 feet from any divers-down warning device. (5) Divers must make reasonable efforts to stay within 300 feet of a divers-down warning device on all waters other than rivers, inlets, and navigation channels. A person operating a vessel on waters other than a river, inlet, or navigation channel must make a reasonable effort to maintain a distance of at least 300 feet from any divers-down warning device.
entries.full: Flag: square or rectangular, symbol on each face; at least 12 in × 12 in displayed from the water; at least 20 in × 24 in displayed from a vessel, with a wire stiffener. Symbol: rectangular or square red symbol with a white diagonal stripe. Buoy: symbol on at least three sides. Vessels forced closer must proceed no faster than is necessary to maintain headway and steerageway. The device must be removed when diving ceases.

entries.title: Fishing from state road bridges
entries.effect: Fishing from a bridge is not prohibited by this statute UNLESS FDOT investigates, finds it dangerous, and posts signs. All three steps are required, so an unposted bridge is presumed to carry the r. 68B-20.003(2)(c) buffer.
entries.excerpt: (1) The Department of Transportation is authorized to investigate and determine whether it is detrimental to traffic safety or dangerous to human life for any person to fish from a state road bridge. When the Department of Transportation, after due investigation, determines that it is dangerous for persons to fish from such a bridge, it shall post appropriate signs on the bridge stating that fishing from the bridge is prohibited. (2) Fishing from a bridge upon which the Department of Transportation has posted signs as provided in subsection (1) is a noncriminal traffic infraction, punishable as a pedestrian violation as provided in chapter 318. (3) This section is cumulative and is not intended to repeal any special law making it unlawful to fish from any bridge.

entries.title: Recreational saltwater fishing licence
entries.effect: Required to take any saltwater organism, and to land saltwater species in Florida regardless of where caught. Spearfishing is fishing.
entries.excerpt: [§ 379.354(1):] Except as provided in s. 379.353, no person shall take game, freshwater or saltwater fish, or fur-bearing animals within this state without having first obtained a license, permit, or authorization number and paid the fees set forth in this chapter. [§ 379.354(4)(k):] An annual resident shoreline fishing license shall be issued without a fee to allow any resident to saltwater fish from land or from a structure fixed to the land. This license is not required for any resident issued any other license identified in this section which allows the taking of saltwater fish.

Exemptions in § 379.353(2), letters verified 29 Sep 2026 for (a), (c), (d), (h), (i), (j), (o): (a) under 16; (c) resident Armed Forces member stationed out of state, home on leave 30 days or less; (d) resident fishing for recreation in the county of residence with live or natural bait on poles or lines without a line retrieval mechanism (cannot cover spearfishing); (h) resident saltwater fishing 'from land or from a structure fixed to the land' who is DCF-eligible for food assistance, temporary cash assistance or Medicaid (does not reach a diver in the water); (i) and (j) fishing from a vessel licensed under § 379.354(7), or whose operator is so licensed; (o) FWC employees and commission-permitted scientific or educational take. The other exemptions listed on 22 Aug (homestead, private ponds, developmental disabilities, commercial licence holders, residents 65 and over, disabled-veteran and active-duty events) were not re-read. Secondary: § 379.354(7)(f) exempts individual scuba divers aboard a vessel that carries divers for a fee when the operator holds the appropriate vessel licence; confirm wording.
entries.note: CORRECTED 29 Sep 2026. The statute gives the shoreline licence only for fishing 'from land or from a structure fixed to the land' and says nothing about swimming or diving. FWC's licence page says the shoreline licence is 'Not valid if taking or attempting to take by swimming or diving' and 'Not valid when fishing from a vessel, or a shoreline reached by vessel'; FWC's FAQ treats a wading angler who can stand on the bottom as fishing from shore. entries.title: Fresh water vs. salt water: where the line falls
entries.effect: Florida's legal test for salt water is a TASTE test, not a salinity number. There is no statewide per-river line and no FWC GIS layer.
entries.excerpt: ‘Salt water,’ except where otherwise provided by law, shall be all of the territorial waters of Florida excluding all lakes, rivers, canals, and other waterways of Florida from such point or points where the fresh and salt waters commingle to such an extent as to become unpalatable because of the saline content, or from such point or points as may be fixed for conservation purposes by the Department of Environmental Protection and the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, with the consent and advice of the board of county commissioners of the county or counties to be affected.
entries.full:
The fresh/salt line matters because it decides which licence you need, which bag limits apply, and whether 68B-4.012's freshwater spearing ban bites.

The operative words are 'unpalatable and unfit for human consumption because of the saline content'. There is NO salinity number anywhere in Florida fisheries law. Closest associated numbers, none of them binding here:

• 1,000 mg/L total dissolved solids — the WHO drinking-water palatability threshold and the USGS fresh/saline divide. This is the best textual match to 'unpalatable', but it is not Florida law and not a fisheries standard.

• 1,500 mg/L chloride, or 4,580 µmhos/cm specific conductance, measured in the bottom half of the water column — Fla. Admin. Code r. 62-302.200(30), the definition of 'predominantly marine waters'. This is the ONLY enforceable numeric salinity line in Florida law, but it belongs to DEP water-quality classification, not to FWC fisheries licensing.

• Only the Steinhatchee River has a designated statutory fresh/salt boundary. FWC publishes no per-river list and no GIS layer. Verified negative.

Novel argument worth knowing: § 379.101(33) drops the words 'and unfit for human consumption' that appear elsewhere, so on its face it triggers on UNPALATABILITY ALONE — a materially lower threshold.

Other states do NOT help: Mississippi, South Carolina and Louisiana all draw geographic lines (I-10, US 17, the Intracoastal Waterway), not salinity lines. Louisiana's legislature expressly rejected salinity as 'insusceptible of precise location by reason of the changes in water salinity caused by winds, tides, and rains.'
entries.note: Practical upshot: in brackish water you cannot know which regime you are in from a meter. Carry both licences, and treat the strictest applicable rule as controlling. This map's inland/tidal/coastal classification is a PLANNING heuristic built from FWC's own ramp labels — it has no legal force. entries.title: Spearguns: manmade canals
entries.effect: Discharging a speargun in any manmade canal in unincorporated Monroe County is unlawful. Conviction forfeits the gun to the Sheriff for destruction.
entries.excerpt:
(a) Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined in this section, on or below the surface of any manmade canal in the unincorporated areas of the county.

(b) Penalties. Any person convicted of a violation of this section shall be penalized in accordance with section 1-8. In addition, any person convicted of a violation of this section shall forfeit the speargun used by such person in committing such offense to the county sheriff for destruction in the same manner as forfeited firearms are disposed of by the sheriff.
entries.full:
§ 26-1 definition: 'Speargun means any device whether commercially manufactured or hand-made, that is designed and constructed so as to be capable of forcefully discharging at great velocity any spear or any similar projectile in a direction determined by the user thereof for a distance greater than two feet (24 inches) whether or not such spear or projectile is tethered to the firing apparatus or otherwise limited in its range. No distinction shall be made as to the mechanical construction or physical means used in such devices to create the potential energy necessary to eject or fire such spear or similar projectiles.'

§ 26-1 also defines: 'Manmade water body means a water body that was created by excavation by mechanical means under human control and shall include a canal, cut basin, or channel where its edges or margins have subsequently been modified by natural forces.'

History: Code 1979, § 13-5; Ord. No. 23-1984, § 1. Monroe code current through Ordinance No. 022-2026, Supp. No. 33 Update 2, 6 Aug 2026.
entries.scope: Manmade canals in UNINCORPORATED Monroe County. The Monroe County State Attorney's Office also lists the City of Marathon as covered.
entries.note:
THE 24-INCH RULE MATTERS: the definition catches any device that can propel a projectile more than two feet, tethered or not, regardless of power source. A pole spear longer than 24 inches of travel, a Hawaiian sling, and a band gun are all caught. Note this is a DISCHARGE ban, not a possession ban — transiting a canal with a stowed gun is not within the operative words.

Also note: most of the Keys above Long Key is already closed by Fla. Stat. § 379.2425 anyway. Read verbatim from Municode 22 Aug 2026. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.cite: Fla. Stat. § 790.33; Fla. Stat. § 379.2425(3); Fla. Admin. Code ch. 68B-3
entries.title: Preemption: § 790.33 covers firearms, not spearguns; the fishing preemption is § 379.2412
entries.effect: Fla. Stat. § 790.33 preempts local regulation of firearms and ammunition and does not reach spearguns. The saltwater fishing preemption is § 379.2412 (entry fs-379-2412), which reserves fish regulation to the state but leaves local governments power over fishing from property they own. Every local ordinance is treated as live.
entries.excerpt: [Fla. Stat. § 379.2425(3):] The Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission shall have the power to establish restricted areas when it is determined that safety hazards exist or when needs are determined by biological findings. Restricted areas shall be established only after an investigation has been conducted and upon application by the governing body of the county or municipality in which the restricted areas are to be located and one publication in a local newspaper of general circulation in said county or municipality in addition to any other notice required by law. [Fla. Stat. § 790.33(1), opening words:] Except as expressly provided by the State Constitution or general law, the Legislature hereby declares that it is occupying the whole field of regulation of firearms and ammunition
entries.full: Fisheries: § 379.2425(3) gives local governments a route to restricted areas by petition to FWC. FAC ch. 68B-3 repeals county fisheries special acts across 30 or more counties, and r. 68B-20.003(8) repeals the spearing special acts of Brevard, Citrus, Collier, Hernando, Hillsborough, Pasco and Sarasota. The direct fishing preemption is § 379.2412 (entry fs-379-2412), which reserves the regulation of saltwater fish to the state and keeps local power over fishing from local government property. Weapons: § 790.33 preempts the field of firearms and ammunition only and says nothing about spearguns; St. Pete Beach § 54-4 carves firearms out of its own speargun ban for that reason. Where FWC expressly declined to repeal an act (Palm Beach chs. 59-1699 and 59-1702, left standing by r. 68B-3.038), an implied-preemption argument is weak. No case law construes any of this. Do not plan a dive around a preemption argument.
entries.note: This map treats every local ordinance as live and enforceable. That is the conservative-with-margin posture the project was built on. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source. CORRECTED 8 Oct 2026: this entry used to present § 790.33 as a preemption vector for spearguns. Its text reaches firearms and ammunition only, and no case construes it to cover spearguns. The fishing preemption statute, § 379.2412, was read verbatim on 7 Oct 2026 and has its own entry.

entries.title: Presidential Security Zone, Palm Beach
entries.effect: Three fixed zones across Lake Worth Lagoon and the adjacent Atlantic at Mar-a-Lago, enforced when protectees are present or expected. Center and East zones: no entering, transiting, anchoring or remaining without COTP authorization. West zone: escorted transit at steady speed only.
entries.excerpt: (1) Center zone. All persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting, anchoring in, or remaining within the security zone unless authorized by the COTP Miami or a designated representative. (2) West zone. All persons and vessels are required to transit the security zone escorted by an on-scene designated representative at a steady speed and may not slow down or stop except in the case of unforeseen mechanical failure or other emergencies. Any persons or vessels forced to slow or stop in the zone shall immediately notify the COTP Miami via VHF channel 16. (3) East zone. All persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting, anchoring in, or remaining within the security zone unless authorized by the COTP Miami or a designated representative.
entries.note: Enforced when the President, First Family or other Secret Service protectees are present or expected. West zone: transit with escort at steady speed. East zone: transit at steady speed, notify if stopping. COTP Miami (305) 535-4472, VHF 16. CORRECTION to earlier project research: Palm Beach has FIXED security zones, not only moving ones. CORRECTED 29 Sep 2026. USCG-2025-0319, 90 FR 42814 (5 Sep 2025, effective that day) made the East zone a no-entry zone. Before that it was steady-speed transit with no stopping, as quoted in the proposed rule (90 FR 30603, 10 Jul 2025). The 22 Aug 2026 note still described the old East zone rule. Enforced when the President, members of the First Family or other Secret Service protectees are present or expected at the Mar-a-Lago Club; the Coast Guard gives notice under 33 C.F.R. § 165.7 and shows flashing blue lights on scene. COTP Miami (305) 535-4472, VHF 16. Palm Beach has FIXED security zones here, not only the moving port zones of § 165.760. History: USCG-2025-0319, 90 FR 42814, effective 5 Sep 2025. The printed East zone Point 2 reads 80°20′9″W, a typo for 80°02′09″W; the map uses 80°02′09″W. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Biscayne National Park bonefish seasonal closed area: no fishing of any kind, 1 March to 31 May
entries.effect: All fishing, spearfishing included, and all possession of fish is prohibited inside a small box of state waters in Biscayne National Park every year from 1 March through 31 May, until 28 February 2031. Transit is allowed with spear shafts out of the gun and all gear secured.
entries.excerpt: Fishing and the possession of fish are prohibited within the Bonefish Seasonal Closed Area, described in paragraph (a), from March 1 through May 31 each year. However, fish or fishing gear may be possessed aboard a vessel, provided such vessel is in continuous transit through the Bonefish Seasonal Closed Area, fishing gear is appropriately stowed, and fish are stowed in a cabin, locker, or similar storage area prior to entering and during transit through the Bonefish Seasonal Closed Area. For the purposes of this subsection, appropriately stowed means hooks cannot be baited, and spear shafts shall not be inserted into any spearing device. All hook-and-line gear, spearing equipment, nets, and other harvesting equipment must be secured in a manner that makes their immediate use impracticable.
entries.full: (5)(a) The Bonefish Seasonal Closed Area shall apply to all state waters located within the following geographic boundary coordinates: [table] Point 1, 25° 27.895' N, 80° 8.800' W; Point 2, 25° 27.588' N, 80° 7.395' W; Point 3, 25° 26.620' N, 80° 7.687' W; Point 4, 25° 26.922' N, 80° 9.100' W. (5)(c) The prohibitions described in paragraph (b) shall only remain in effect through February 28, 2031. However, the Commission shall review the seasonal closure prior to that date and determine whether repeal is appropriate or if the closure should be renewed or modfied. [sic] Definition, r. 68B-7.002(3): "Fishing" means: (a) The catching, taking, or harvesting of fish; (b) The attempted catching, taking, or harvesting of fish; or (c) Any other activity which can reasonably be expected to result in the catching, taking, or harvesting of fish. R. 68B-7.001: "The regulations in this chapter apply in all state and federal waters of Biscayne National Park."
entries.scope: Quadrilateral of about 1.74 sq mi (area as stated in the notice of proposed rule): 25.46492 N 80.14667 W; 25.45980 N 80.12325 W; 25.44367 N 80.12812 W; 25.44870 N 80.15167 W. State waters within the box only, per (5)(a).
entries.note: NEW 29 Sep 2026. Effective 4 Nov 2025 (history: New 7-1-20, Amended 4-1-23, 11-4-25), so it was already in force when the 22 Aug 2026 registry said ch. 68B-7 has no spear prohibition. Proposed as a hook-and-line-only closure from 1 Nov to 31 May (FAR Vol. 51 No. 137, 16 Jul 2025, p. 2651); the notice of change (FAR Vol. 51 No. 184, 22 Sep 2025, p. 3573) widened it to all fishing and possession, moved the start to 1 March, added the spearing-equipment stowage sentence and moved the sunset to 28 Feb 2031. Part of the box may lie outside the 3 nm state-waters line; the map should draw the whole box (conservative reading). Datum not stated in the text read. entries.title: Marine life fish, including every triggerfish except gray and ocean: spears are not on the gear list
entries.effect: Tropical ornamental fish, which include every triggerfish and filefish except gray triggerfish, ocean triggerfish and unicorn filefish, may be harvested only with hand nets, barrier nets, drop nets and slurp guns. Spearing one (a queen triggerfish, for example) is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: [r. 68B-42.001(2)(bb):] Filefish/triggerfish - Any species of the Family Balistidae, except gray triggerfish, Balistes capriscus, ocean triggerfish, Canthidermis sufflamen, and unicorn filefish, Aluterus monoceros. [r. 68B-42.007(3):] No person shall harvest in or from state waters any tropical fish by or with the use of any gear other than those types specified in subsection (1);
entries.full: R. 68B-42.001(2), lead-in: "The following fish species, as they occur in waters of the state and in federal Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) waters adjacent to state waters, are hereby designated as restricted species pursuant to Section 379.101(32), F.S.:" R. 68B-42.001(5): "For the purposes of Section 379.361(2)(j), F.S., the term "marine life species" is defined to mean those species designated as restricted species in subsections (2), (3), and (4), of this rule." R. 68B-42.002(18): "Tropical fish" means any species included in subsection (2) of Rule 68B-42.001, F.A.C., or any part thereof. R. 68B-42.007(1): "The following types of gear shall be the only types allowed for the harvest of any tropical fish, whether from state waters or from federal Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) waters adjacent to state waters:" followed by (a) to (g), paraphrased: hand held net, barrier net, drop net, slurp gun, quinaldine (licensed), roller frame trawl (shrimp bycatch), dwarf seahorse trawl. (2) permits a single blunt rod used with allowable gear. The rest of (3) excuses commercial incidental bycatch within the r. 68B-42.005 bag limit.
entries.scope: State waters and, for the gear list in (1), adjacent federal EEZ waters.
entries.note: NEW 29 Sep 2026. R. 68B-42.001 last amended 1 Nov 2012; r. 68B-42.007 last amended 14 Aug 2024. entries.title: Warsaw Hole / 50 Fathom Hole spawning SMZ: no snapper-grouper by any gear, no anchoring
entries.effect: A square about 1.3 nm on a side, roughly 25 nm west-southwest of Key West, where no snapper-grouper may be taken by any gear (spear included) and a fishing vessel may not anchor, until 2 Aug 2027 unless extended.
entries.excerpt: Any fishing vessel in a spawning SMZ is prohibited to fish for or harvest species in the snapper-grouper fishery management unit year-round. For a fishing vessel to possess snapper-grouper species on board while in a spawning SMZ, the vessel must be in transit and fishing gear must be appropriately stowed, as specified in paragraph (a)(2)(vii) of this section. Except for spawning SMZs of Area 51 and Area 53, the spawning SMZs in this paragraph are effective until August 2, 2027. A person on board a fishing vessel may not anchor, use an anchor and chain, or use a grapple and chain while in the spawning SMZs specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section. The anchoring prohibition does not apply to fishing vessels in the spawning SMZs of Area 51 and Area 53.
entries.scope: Warsaw Hole/50 Fathom Hole Spawning SMZ, § 622.183(a)(2)(vi): rhumb lines A 24°22.277′N 82°20.417′W, B 24°22.277′N 82°18.215′W, C 24°20.932′N 82°18.215′W, D 24°20.932′N 82°20.417′W, back to A. The only one of the five spawning SMZs off Florida (the others are off North and South Carolina).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. SUNSET: the Warsaw Hole SMZ is effective until 2 Aug 2027. The SAFMC is developing Snapper Grouper Regulatory Amendment 39 on the sunsetting of spawning SMZs (council meeting notices, Federal Register 18 Feb, 21 May, 17 Aug and 28 Aug 2026). Re-check after the SAFMC acts and before 2 Aug 2027. Regulatory Amendment 36 (final rule 91 FR, 28 Sep 2026, doc. 2026-19801, effective 28 Oct 2026) revises the transit gear-stowage text in (a)(2)(vii) for sea bass pots only; no effect on divers. 'Fishing vessel' is not defined in part 622; the conservative reading treats any boat carrying a spearfisher as a fishing vessel for the anchoring ban. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Florida artificial-reef SMZs: spearfishing banned at Ft. Pierce Inshore and Key Biscayne AR-H
entries.effect: Two federal artificial-reef SMZs off Florida ban spearfishing gear outright (Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef, Key Biscayne/Artificial Reef H). A third, Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef, restricts reels, sea bass pots and bottom longlines, and its table row contains no spearfishing restriction.
entries.excerpt: (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xxi): Use of spearfishing gear is prohibited.
entries.full: To determine what restrictions apply in the SMZs listed in paragraph (a)(1) of this section, follow this table: (a)(1)(i) through (x) and (a)(1)(xxii) through (xxxix): Use of a powerhead to take South Atlantic snapper-grouper is prohibited. Possession of a powerhead and a mutilated South Atlantic snapper-grouper in, or after having fished in, one of these SMZs constitutes prima facie evidence that such fish was taken with a powerhead in the SMZ. Harvest and possession of a South Atlantic snapper-grouper is limited to the bag limits specified in § 622.187(b). (a)(1)(i) through (xviii) and (a)(1)(xxii) through (li): Fishing may only be conducted with handline, rod and reel, and spearfishing gear. (a)(1)(i) through (li): Use of a sea bass pot or bottom longline is prohibited. (a)(1)(xii) through (xviii) and (a)(1)(xl) through (li): Possession of South Atlantic snapper-grouper taken with a powerhead is limited to the bag limits specified in § 622.187(b). (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xx): A hydraulic or electric reel that is permanently affixed to the vessel is prohibited when fishing for South Atlantic snapper-grouper. (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xxi): Use of spearfishing gear is prohibited.
entries.scope: Only three of the 51 South Atlantic SMZs lie off Florida: (xix) Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef, N 27°26.8′, S 27°25.8′, E 80°09.24′W, W 80°10.36′W; (xx) Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef, A 27°23.68′N 80°03.95′W, B 27°22.80′N 80°03.60′W, C 27°23.94′N 80°00.02′W, D 27°24.85′N 80°00.33′W; (xxi) Key Biscayne/Artificial Reef H, N 25°42.82′, S 25°41.32′, E 80°04.22′W, W 80°05.53′W. (xlvi) Artificial Reef KBY and (xlviii) Artificial Reef MRY lie just north of the Florida/Georgia line (30°45.5′N to 30°48.6′N) and allow handline, rod and reel and spearfishing gear only.

The spearfishing row in table 2 is not limited to snapper-grouper on its face, so it is drawn as a ban on all spearfishing inside (xix) and (xxi) (the reading that closes more water). The powerhead ban row covers (i) to (x) and (xxii) to (xxxix) only, none off Florida. Row applying to (i) to (li): 'Use of a sea bass pot or bottom longline is prohibited.' The Key Biscayne box's west edge is about 3 nm off the beach; check whether any part lies in state waters.
