entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ: no spearing snapper-grouper while on a rebreather
entries.effect: In federal waters off the Florida east coast and Keys, a diver on a rebreather may not spear any snapper-grouper species; open-circuit scuba and freediving are unaffected.
entries.excerpt: (b) Rebreathers and spearfishing gear. In the South Atlantic EEZ, a person using a rebreather may not harvest South Atlantic snapper-grouper with spearfishing gear. The possession of such snapper-grouper while in the water with a rebreather is prima facie evidence that such fish was harvested with spearfishing gear while using a rebreather.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ only (east coast of Florida and the Atlantic side of the Keys). No equivalent rule in the Gulf EEZ: an eCFR title 50 search for 'rebreather' returns only this section.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Snapper-grouper species list is table 2 of appendix A to part 622 (includes hogfish, groupers, snappers, black sea bass, triggerfish, amberjacks, porgies). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Hogfish closed in federal waters off the Keys and east coast, November through April
entries.effect: No recreational hogfish harvest or possession from the federal waters off the Keys and the Florida east coast (and Gulf federal waters south of 25°09′N) in January to April and November to December.
entries.excerpt: Hogfish recreational sector off the Florida Keys and east coast of Florida. From January through April and from November through December each year, the recreational harvest or possession of hogfish in or from the South Atlantic EEZ off the Florida Keys and east coast of Florida, and in the Gulf EEZ south of 25°09′ N. lat. off the west coast of Florida is prohibited, and the bag and possession limits are zero.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ off the Keys and east coast; Gulf EEZ south of 25°09′N. Size limit 16 inches fork length in the same waters, § 622.185(c)(3)(ii). § 622.34(g) cross-refers here for the Gulf portion.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Hogfish is taken almost entirely by spear, so this is a spearfishing season in practice. State-water hogfish seasons are set separately by FWC; compare regs.json 'seasons' before publishing. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Goliath, Nassau, speckled hind and warsaw grouper: no harvest in federal waters
entries.effect: These four groupers may not be taken or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ (Nassau also in the Gulf EEZ), by any gear including spear.
entries.excerpt: Goliath grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ. [...] Speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ. [...] Nassau grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ.
entries.full: (b)(1) Goliath grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ. Goliath grouper taken in the South Atlantic EEZ incidentally by hook-and-line must be released immediately by cutting the line without removing the fish from the water. (b)(3) Speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ. Such fish caught in the South Atlantic EEZ must be released immediately with a minimum of harm. These restrictions also apply in the South Atlantic on board a vessel for which a valid Federal commercial or charter vessel/headboat permit for South Atlantic snapper-grouper has been issued, i.e., in state or Federal waters. (b)(4) Nassau grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ. Nassau grouper taken in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ incidentally by hook-and-line must be released immediately by cutting the line without removing the fish from the water.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ; Nassau grouper also Gulf EEZ. The Gulf goliath grouper rule was not located in § 622.32 (which only bans poisons); find its current section before citing a Gulf goliath prohibition.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Goliath grouper has a limited state-water harvest by FWC permit since 2023; the federal EEZ prohibition is unchanged. Speckled hind and warsaw grouper restrictions also apply in state waters aboard a vessel with a federal snapper-grouper commercial or charter permit ((b)(3) last sentence). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ: descending device must be aboard, spearfishing boats included
entries.effect: A boat whose divers are spearing or holding snapper-grouper in South Atlantic federal waters must carry a rigged descending device; the text has no spearfishing exemption.
entries.excerpt: (4) Descending device. At least one descending device is required to be on board a vessel and be ready for use while fishing for or possessing South Atlantic snapper-grouper.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Not a closure, an equipment rule. The text does not exempt spearfishing; the conservative reading is that it applies. § 622.188(b) lists spearfishing gear among the only authorized gear types for snapper-grouper. The Gulf equivalent, § 622.30(c) (DESCEND Act), states it was 'effective until January 14, 2026' and has lapsed; NOAA Fisheries' action page (read 30 Sep 2026, secondary) says a framework action to continue it was proposed 30 Jul 2026. Currency watch. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Oculina experimental closed area: no snapper-grouper, spear included
entries.effect: Inside the Oculina Bank HAPC, the box from 27°30′N to 27°53′N and 79°56′W to 80°00′W is closed to fishing for snapper-grouper by any gear, spearfishing included, and none may be retained.
entries.excerpt: Within the Oculina Bank HAPC, the experimental closed area is bounded on the north by 27°53′ N. lat., on the south by 27°30′ N. lat., on the east by 79°56′ W. long., and on the west by 80°00' W. long. No person may fish for South Atlantic snapper-grouper in the experimental closed area, and no person may retain South Atlantic snapper-grouper in or from the area.
entries.scope: Off Fort Pierce and Vero Beach, 60 to 100 m depth; inside the Oculina Bank HAPC so the HAPC anchoring ban also applies.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Split out of cfr-622-224 because that entry's effect ('NOT a spearfishing closure') is wrong for this paragraph. The eCFR prints the west bound as 80°00' with a straight apostrophe; reproduced as printed. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Dolphin and wahoo: spearfishing, powerheads included, is authorized gear in the Atlantic EEZ
entries.effect: For dolphin (mahi) and wahoo in Atlantic federal waters, the gear rule does not exclude spears, and it expressly lists powerheads for these two species.
entries.excerpt: Except as allowed in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, the following are the only authorized gear types in the fishery for dolphin and wahoo in the Atlantic EEZ: Automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, pelagic longline, rod and reel, and spearfishing gear (including powerheads).
entries.scope: Atlantic EEZ.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Kept as a positive rule because divers ask. 50 C.F.R. § 600.725(v) lists spear and powerhead for the South Atlantic snapper-grouper and Gulf reef fish recreational fisheries too (see cfr-600-725). For king and Spanish mackerel and cobia see cfr-622-375-a. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Federal list of authorized gear: spear and powerhead listed for recreational reef fish
entries.effect: Spearfishing is an authorized federal recreational gear for South Atlantic snapper-grouper, Gulf reef fish and coastal migratory pelagics; a spear used on king or Spanish mackerel in the Atlantic is outside the § 622.375 gear list but the only consequence is that the bag limit applies.
entries.excerpt: South Atlantic Fishery Management Council ... 8. South Atlantic Coastal Migratory Pelagics Fishery (FMP): ... D. Recreational fishery | D. Bandit gear, rod and reel, handline, spear. Gulf Fishery Management Council ... 5. Gulf Coastal Migratory Pelagics Fishery (FMP): ... E. Recreational fishery | E. Bandit gear, handline, rod and reel, spear.
entries.scope: Federal EEZ, South Atlantic and Gulf councils.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 from the eCFR versioner API (version of 6 Oct 2026; current version effective 6 Apr 2026). Paragraph (v) opening: 'The list of fisheries and authorized gear does not, in any way, alter or supersede any definitions or regulations contained elsewhere in this chapter. A person or vessel is prohibited from engaging in fishing or employing fishing gear when such fishing gear is prohibited or restricted by regulation under an FMP or other applicable law.' So § 622.375(a)(1) controls for king and Atlantic Spanish mackerel. The snapper-grouper and Gulf reef fish recreational rows previously quoted from govinfo 2025 were not re-read this pass; re-check them before relying on the old excerpt text, which this replaces.

entries.title: King mackerel: spear is not an authorized federal gear (Atlantic south of Cape Lookout, and Gulf)
entries.effect: In federal waters off Florida a spear is not on the gear list for king mackerel (Atlantic or Gulf group) or Atlantic-group Spanish mackerel; a diver who spears one is held to the recreational bag limit, which is the limit a recreational diver has anyway.
entries.excerpt: (1) King and Spanish mackerel. Subject to the prohibitions on gear/methods specified in § 622.9, the following are the only fishing gears that may be used in the Gulf, Mid-Atlantic, and South Atlantic EEZ in directed fisheries for king and Spanish mackerel: (i) King mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—[...] (B) South of 34°37.3′ N. lat.—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, and rod and reel. (ii) King mackerel, Gulf migratory group—hook-and-line gear and, in the southern zone only, run-around gillnet. [...] (iii) Spanish mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, rod and reel, cast net, run-around gillnet, and stab net. (iv) Spanish mackerel, Gulf migratory group—all gear except drift gillnet, long gillnet, and purse seine.
entries.scope: Gulf, Mid-Atlantic and South Atlantic EEZ. Gulf-group cobia ((a)(2), which covers the Gulf EEZ and the South Atlantic EEZ south of a line due east from the Florida/Georgia border): all gear except drift gillnet and long gillnet, so spearing cobia is authorized.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (b)(3): 'Except as specified in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, a person aboard a vessel with unauthorized gear other than a drift gillnet in the Gulf EEZ or a long gillnet on board in, or that has fished in, the EEZ where such gear is not authorized in paragraph (a) of this section, is subject to the bag limits for king and Spanish mackerel specified in § 622.382(a)(1)(ii) and (iv), respectively, and to the limit on cobia specified in § 622.383(b).' CONFLICT to flag: § 600.725(v) (govinfo 2025 edition) lists 'spear' as authorized gear for the South Atlantic and Gulf coastal migratory pelagics recreational fisheries. 'Directed fisheries' is undefined in § 622.375. Practical reading for the map: spearing king or Atlantic Spanish mackerel in the EEZ is not a closure; the consequence is the bag limit. Not a map feature; a sidebar note. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source. Re-read 7 Oct 2026 from the eCFR versioner API (version of 6 Oct 2026); last amended 21 Mar 2019, unchanged. (b)(3) verbatim as previously recorded. The current § 600.725(v) (effective 6 Apr 2026) lists spear for SA and Gulf CMP recreational fisheries but states the list does not 'alter or supersede' other regulations in the chapter, so this section controls. 'Directed fisheries' remains undefined. Conservative reading kept: spearing Atlantic king, Gulf king or Atlantic Spanish mackerel in the EEZ is not authorized gear; stated consequence is the bag limit. Gulf-group Spanish mackerel and Gulf-group cobia: the federal gear rule does not exclude spear.

entries.cite: 50 C.F.R. § 622.35(a)(1); app. B to pt. 622, table 2
entries.title: Gulf reef fish stressed area: no powerheads (spearguns fine)
entries.effect: In the band of Gulf federal waters between state waters and a line running from the Tortugas to the Alabama line, powerheads may not be used on reef fish; ordinary spearguns are not restricted.
entries.excerpt: (1) A powerhead may not be used in the stressed area to take Gulf reef fish. Possession of a powerhead and a mutilated Gulf reef fish in the stressed area or after having fished in the stressed area constitutes prima facie evidence that such reef fish was taken with a powerhead in the stressed area.
entries.scope: 'The stressed area is that part of the Gulf EEZ shoreward of rhumb lines connecting, in order, the points listed in Table 2 in Appendix B of this part.' Florida points 1 to 15: 1 24°45.5′N 82°41.5′W (NE of Dry Tortugas) through 15 29°34.5′N 87°38.0′W (south of the Florida and Alabama border).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Powerhead is defined at § 622.2: 'any device with an explosive charge, usually attached to a speargun, spear, pole, or stick, that fires a projectile upon contact.' Map as a line with a warn popup; the landward edge is the state waters boundary (9 nm off the Gulf coast). The only other Gulf spearfishing text in § 622.35 is the Alabama SMZ (d), which lies wholly off Alabama (easternmost point 87°55.5′W, west of the Florida line): confirmed negative for Florida. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Gulf coral HAPCs off Florida: NOT a spearfishing rule, but some ban anchoring
entries.effect: Florida Middle Grounds bans only bottom longline, trawl, dredge, pot and trap; Tortugas North and South ban all fishing and anchoring by fishing vessels; Pulley Ridge South, Pulley Ridge South Portion A and West Florida Wall ban bottom gear and anchoring by fishing vessels.
entries.excerpt: Deployment of a bottom longline, bottom trawl, dredge, pot, or trap is prohibited year-round in the area bounded by rhumb lines connecting the following points in order: [Florida Middle Grounds HAPC, (a)]
entries.scope: Florida Middle Grounds (a): A 28°42.500′N 84°24.800′W, B 28°42.500′N 84°16.300′W, C 28°11.000′N 84°00.000′W, D 28°11.000′N 84°07.000′W, E 28°26.600′N 84°24.800′W. Pulley Ridge South (c), Pulley Ridge South Portion A (d), West Florida Wall (e), Tortugas marine reserves HAPC (b). Coordinates in geometry.json.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Intro text: 'For the purposes of this section, fishing gear is deployed if any part of the gear is in contact with the water.' (b): 'Fishing for any species and bottom anchoring by fishing vessels are prohibited year-round in the areas of the HAPC.' (c): 'Deployment of a bottom longline, bottom trawl, buoy gear, dredge, pot, or trap, and bottom anchoring by fishing vessels are prohibited year-round in the area of the HAPC bounded by rhumb lines connecting the following points in order:' The Florida Middle Grounds has NO anchoring ban and no diver rule, a confirmed negative worth stating because it is a popular spearfishing destination. § 622.74(b)(1) cites NOAA chart 11434 for the Tortugas North state-waters edge while § 622.410(a) cites chart 11438: an inconsistency inside the CFR. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Highly migratory species: spearguns only for yellowfin, bigeye, albacore and skipjack tuna
entries.effect: In federal waters a speargun may be used on BAYS tunas (bigeye, albacore, yellowfin, skipjack) only, from a boat with an HMS Angling or Charter/Headboat permit, diver in the water, no powerheads; spearing bluefin tuna, billfish, swordfish or sharks is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: (h) Speargun fishing gear. Speargun fishing gear may only be utilized when recreational fishing for Atlantic BAYS tunas and only from vessels issued either a valid HMS Angling or valid HMS Charter/Headboat permit. Persons fishing for Atlantic BAYS tunas using speargun gear, as specified in § 635.19, must be physically in the water when the speargun is fired or discharged, and may freedive, use SCUBA, or other underwater breathing devices. Only free-swimming BAYS tunas, not those restricted by fishing lines or other means, may be taken by speargun fishing gear. "Powerheads," as defined at § 600.10 of this chapter, or any other explosive devices, may not be used to harvest or fish for BAYS tunas with speargun fishing gear.
entries.full: § 635.71(b)(30) Fish for any HMS, other than Atlantic BAYS tunas, with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.21(h). (31) Harvest or fish for BAYS tunas using speargun gear with powerheads, or any other explosive devices, as specified in § 635.21(h). (32) Sell, purchase, barter for, or trade for an Atlantic BAYS tuna harvested with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.31(a)(1). (33) Fire or discharge speargun gear without being physically in the water, as specified at § 635.21(h). (34) Use speargun gear to harvest a BAYS tuna restricted by fishing lines or other means, as specified at § 635.21(h). (35) Use speargun gear to fish for BAYS tunas from a vessel that does not possess either a valid HMS Angling or HMS Charter/Headboat category permit, as specified at § 635.21(h).
entries.scope: Atlantic HMS management area, which includes the Gulf and Caribbean. Speargun fishing gear is defined at § 635.2 as a muscle-powered speargun with a trigger, a spear designed to penetrate and retain fish, and terminal gear.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. § 635.71(b)(30): 'Fish for any HMS, other than Atlantic BAYS tunas, with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.21(h).' (b)(32): BAYS tuna taken by speargun may not be sold. § 635.19(c) billfish and sailfish: rod and reel only; (d) sharks: rod and reel or handline only; (e) swordfish (recreational): handline or rod and reel only. This matches the state ban on spearing sharks and billfish in r. 68B-20.005. Federal HMS permit and tuna reporting obligations apply to the vessel. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Spiny lobster: no spears or hooks in federal waters
entries.effect: A spiny lobster may not be speared or hooked in federal waters, and a speared or punctured lobster aboard is presumed illegally taken.
entries.excerpt: A spiny lobster may not be taken in the EEZ with a spear, hook, or similar device, or gear containing such devices. In the EEZ, the possession of a speared, pierced, or punctured spiny lobster is prima facie evidence that prohibited gear was used to take such lobster.
entries.scope: Gulf and South Atlantic EEZ (subpart R, spiny lobster fishery). Part 697 (American lobster) also bans spearing, § 697.7, but American lobster does not occur off Florida.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Mirrors the state prohibition. The remaining sentence of (a) excludes a hook in a hook-and-line fishery for other species. Paragraph (e) bans simultaneous possession of a bully net and underwater breathing apparatus aboard a commercial lobster vessel in the EEZ off Florida (commercial only). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Refuges not listed in part 32 are closed to fishing, including spearfishing
entries.effect: Taking any animal on a national wildlife refuge is prohibited unless part 32 opens that refuge; sixteen Florida refuges are opened and the rest (Key West, Great White Heron, National Key Deer, Crystal River, Crocodile Lake, Passage Key, Pine Island, Matlacha Pass, Island Bay, Archie Carr, among others) are not.
entries.excerpt: No person shall take any animal or plant on any national wildlife refuge, except as authorized under 50 CFR 27.51 and parts 31, 32, and 33 of this subchapter C.
entries.scope: § 32.7(i) Florida list: Arthur R. Marshall Loxahatchee, Cedar Keys, Chassahowitzka, Egmont Key, Everglades Headwaters, Florida Panther, Hobe Sound, J.N. "Ding" Darling, Lake Woodruff, Lower Suwannee, Merritt Island, Pelican Island, Pinellas, St. Marks, St. Vincent, Ten Thousand Islands.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. CONFLICT, unresolved: the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's own Key West NWR and Great White Heron NWR pages (fws.gov, read 30 Sep 2026) say 'Sport and commercial fishing in accordance with state fishing laws' and that refuge waters are open 24 hours for fishing, snorkeling and diving. The submerged lands there are state-owned and co-managed under the 1992 Backcountry Management Agreement, so they may not be refuge 'waters administered by FWS' within § 25.12. Drawn as warn, not closed, with this conflict stated; the conservative reading (closed) rests on the CFR text alone. Passage Key NWR, Pine Island NWR, Matlacha Pass NWR, Island Bay NWR and Crocodile Lake NWR are posted by FWS as closed to the public; for Pine Island, Matlacha Pass and Island Bay the refuge is the islands, and the surrounding water is a state aquatic preserve (FWS pages), so the water is not closed by the refuge. § 26.21(a): 'No person shall trespass, including but not limited to entering, occupying, using, or being upon, any national wildlife refuge, except as specifically authorized in this subchapter C or in other applicable Federal regulations.' Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source. Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: § 32.28 last amended 30 Oct 2023; 'Key West' and 'Great White Heron' do not appear in § 32.28; § 32.7(i) still lists 16 Florida refuges, neither of these. The 2026 to 2027 station-specific rule (91 FR 56290, 1 Sep 2026; correction 91 FR 60900, 25 Sep 2026) contains no Florida, 32.28 or refuge-name text. CONFLICT unchanged: fws.gov Key West and Great White Heron pages (read 7 Oct 2026): 'The refuge waters are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year for water-based activities such as boating, fishing, wildlife viewing, photography, snorkeling and diving.' and 'Sport and commercial fishing in accordance with state fishing laws.' Both pages state the submerged lands are managed by the State of Florida under the 1992 Management Agreement. Drawn warn. Passage Key and Pinellas pages: closed to all public use year-round (islands).

entries.title: Hobe Sound NWR: rods and reels and poles and lines only, so no spearfishing
entries.effect: Fishing on Hobe Sound NWR (including its Jupiter Island beach) is limited to rods and reels and poles and lines, sunrise to sunset, which excludes spearfishing from refuge lands and waters.
entries.excerpt: (iii) We allow the use of only rods and reels and poles and lines, and anglers must attend them at all times.
entries.scope: Hobe Sound NWR, Martin County: Jupiter Island beach unit and Indian River Lagoon mainland unit. The refuge's seaward boundary was not checked; if it stops at mean high water, the rule governs shore entry through the refuge rather than the water itself.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (g)(4)(i): 'We allow fishing only from legal sunrise to legal sunset.' (ii): 'We allow salt-water fishing along the Atlantic Ocean and Indian River Lagoon year-round as governed by State recreational fishing regulations.' Conservative reading: a diver who enters from the refuge beach and spears is using a non-authorized gear on the refuge. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: J.N. "Ding" Darling NWR: no bows or spears from Wildlife Drive
entries.effect: Spears may not be used from Wildlife Drive or any trail or structure attached to it; the rule does not ban spearfishing elsewhere in refuge waters, but anglers must leave refuge waters by half an hour after sunset and fish must stay whole.
entries.excerpt: (vi) We prohibit the use of bows and spears from Wildlife Drive or any trail or structure affixed to Wildlife Drive.
entries.scope: J.N. "Ding" Darling NWR, Sanibel Island, Lee County.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (h)(4)(ii): 'All anglers must exit refuge lands and waters no later than 1/2 hour after legal sunset.' (v): 'All fish must remain in whole condition until removed from refuge lands and waters, [...]'. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Pinellas NWR: fishing only from vessels around Tarpon Key
entries.effect: The only fishing Pinellas NWR allows is from vessels in the waters around Tarpon Key; an in-water spearfisher is not fishing from a vessel, so the conservative reading treats refuge waters as closed to spearfishing.
entries.excerpt: (4) Sport fishing. We allow sport fishing year-round on designated areas of the refuge subject to the following condition: We allow fishing only from vessels in the waters surrounding Tarpon Key.
entries.scope: Pinellas NWR, lower Tampa Bay (Tarpon, Mule, Listen and other keys). Water boundary not checked.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Ambiguity stated: 'from vessels' could be read as a mode-of-access rule rather than a gear rule. Drawn as the reading that closes more water. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Cedar Keys NWR: 300-foot buffer around Snake Key closed to all entry, 1 March to 30 June
entries.effect: Water within 300 feet of Snake Key's mean high tide line is closed to all public entry from 1 March through 30 June; Seahorse Key's buffer closes if birds nest.
entries.excerpt: (i) We close a 300-foot (90-meter (m)) buffer zone beginning at mean high tide line and extending into the waters around Snake Key to all public entry from March 1 through June 30 to protect nesting birds.
entries.scope: Snake Key and Seahorse Key, Cedar Keys NWR, Levy County.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (ii): 'We conditionally open to public entry a 300-foot (90-m) buffer zone beginning at mean high tide line and extending into the waters around Seahorse Key from March 1 through June 30. Should birds nest in that area during that timeframe, we will close that area of Seahorse Key to public entry.' Geometry would be a 300-ft (91.44 m) buffer of a mean-high-water shoreline; no such shoreline is in hand, so no polygon is proposed. Marker only. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Merritt Island NWR: refuge fishing permit required; night fishing only from a vessel
entries.effect: Anyone fishing (spearfishing included) on Merritt Island NWR must carry the signed refuge fishing permit; fishing is daylight only except from a vessel in the open lagoons, and Kennedy Space Center restricted areas are off limits.
entries.excerpt: (i) You must possess a current, signed refuge fishing permit (signed brochure) at all times while fishing on the refuge.
entries.scope: Merritt Island NWR, Brevard and Volusia Counties: Mosquito Lagoon, Indian River Lagoon, Banana River, Haulover Canal.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (ii): 'We prohibit anglers entering the normal or expanded restricted areas of the Kennedy Space Center (KSC).' (iii): 'We prohibit fishing after legal sunset or before legal sunrise, except that we allow fishing at night from a vessel in the open waters of Mosquito Lagoon, Indian River Lagoon, Banana River, and Haulover Canal.' (x) Banana River No-Motor Zone. (xiii): no fishing from or near the Haulover Canal Manatee Viewing Deck. No gear list, so spearfishing is not excluded by the refuge rule; state inland-waters spearing rules (r. 68B-20.003, Volusia rule) still apply. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Egmont Key NWR: two attended poles per angler
entries.effect: Egmont Key NWR's only fishing condition is two attended poles per angler; whether that excludes a spear is ambiguous, and the conservative reading treats refuge waters as closed to spearfishing.
entries.excerpt: (4) Sport fishing. We allow sport fishing year-round on designated areas of the refuge subject to the following condition: Anglers may only use two poles per angler and must attend both poles at all times.
entries.scope: Egmont Key NWR, mouth of Tampa Bay (co-managed with Egmont Key State Park).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Ambiguous: the text limits pole count but does not say poles are the only gear. Refuge water boundary not checked. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Dry Tortugas Research Natural Area: closed to all fishing and anchoring
entries.effect: The 46-square-mile Research Natural Area in the northwest of the park is closed to all fishing, anchoring is banned, and boats must use the mooring buoys.
entries.excerpt: The following waters and areas are closed to fishing: (i) The Research Natural Area (RNA): Fish and fishing gear may be possessed aboard a vessel in the RNA, provided such fish can be shown not to have been harvested from within, removed from, or taken within the RNA, as applicable, by being stowed in a cabin, locker, or similar storage area prior to entering and during transit through the RNA, provided further that such vessel is in continuous transit through the RNA.
entries.scope: (a)(14): 'Research Natural Area (RNA) at Dry Tortugas National Park means the 46-square-statute-mile area in the northwest portion of the park enclosed by connecting with straight lines the adjacent points of 82°51′ W and 24°36′ N, and 82°58′ W and 24°36′ N west to the park boundary, but excluding: (i) The designated anchorage; (ii) Garden Key, Bush Key and Long Key; or (iii) The central portion of Loggerhead key including the lighthouse and associated buildings.'
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (e)(1) 'Anchoring in the Research Natural Area (RNA) is prohibited.' (e)(2) 'All vessels in the RNA must use designated mooring buoys.' (h)(1): a Superintendent's permit is required for all non-commercial vessels whose occupants are engaged in recreational activities, including all activities in the RNA. (b)(3)(ii) to (v) also close the Garden Key moat, buoyed swim and snorkel areas, within 50 feet of the historic coaling docks, and helipad areas. Compendium (last updated 31 Aug 2026, secondary): no fishing from Bush Key; no fishing from the Garden Key dock when the ferry is docked; diving between sunset and sunrise outside 1 nm of the Garden Key Light needs a permit; no entering or exiting the water from the moat wall. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.cite: Biscayne National Park Superintendent's Compendium (approved 17 Sep 2025), 36 CFR 2.1, 3.16 and 3.18
entries.title: Biscayne NP: no diving or snorkeling within 100 feet of marked channels, in named harbors, or at Legare Anchorage
entries.effect: Swimming, snorkeling and diving are closed within 100 feet of every marked navigational channel in the park, in three harbors and two harbor mouths, and in the Legare Anchorage box (25°29′N to 25°30′N, 80°07′W to 80°08′W).
entries.excerpt: The following areas are closed to swimming, wading, snorkeling, and underwater diving: The Legare Anchorage within the rectangular area bounded by latitude 25°30 N and 25°29 N and longitude 80°08 W and 80°07 W; Boca Chita Key Harbor; Elliott Key Harbor; Convoy Point Harbor; Within the slow speed zone at the mouth/entrance of Boca Chita Key Harbor; Within the mouth/entrance of Elliott Key Harbor; Within one hundred feet (100') of all marked navigational channels
entries.scope: Biscayne National Park. The 100-foot channel buffer applies park-wide; geometry would need the park's aids-to-navigation or channel layer.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Legare Anchorage (36 CFR 2.1): 'For the protection of artifacts, the portion of Biscayne National Park known as the Legare Anchorage within the area bounded by latitude 25°30 N and 25°29 N and longitude 80°08 W and 80°07 W is closed to the following activities: Scuba diving, snorkeling, swimming, floating, and any activity that involves placing persons or equipment, on, in or under water. However, hook and line "drift" fishing is allowed. Use of any underwater viewing device including, but not limited to, face masks, glass bottom boats, glass bottom buckets or cameras. Anchoring any vessel at any time unless an emergency.' The compendium does not mention bonefish or r. 68B-7.008; the bonefish closure is state law only. The 100-foot channel rule is new to the registry and closes more water than the six fishing spots in bnp-status. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.cite: Gulf Islands National Seashore Superintendent's Compendium (2021 onward), 36 CFR 1.5; park fishing pages
entries.title: Gulf Islands NS: the current compendium (1 Sep 2026) has no spearfishing or projectile-gear rule
entries.effect: The Superintendent's Compendium last updated 1 Sep 2026 contains no provision on spears, spearguns, Hawaiian slings or projectile gear and has no section 2.3, so it adds no spearfishing closure of its own; under 36 CFR 2.3(e) and 2.4(b)(2)(i)(B), Florida's spearfishing rules and closures govern Seashore salt water. Fishing is closed at the Fort Pickens and Ship Island ferry docks, the Davis Bayou boat ramp dock, the Ship Island boardwalk and the designated swim beaches when lifeguards are on duty, and diving is prohibited within 200 feet of the Fort Pickens fishing pier. The 2021 projectile ban is not in the current text, but two stale nps.gov pages still state it: call the park (850-934-2600) to confirm it was rescinded.
entries.excerpt: Section 1.5(a)(1): Fishing Closures a. Fishing and cast netting from public boat docks and boardwalks are not allowed in the following areas: 1. Fort Pickens and Ship Island ferry docks, 2. Davis Bayou boat ramp dock, 3. Ship Island cross island boardwalk, 4. In the small ponds and small creeks within the Davis Bayou area.
entries.scope: Water boundary, verbatim from the NPS 'Fishing in Florida' page: In the Perdido Key, Fort Pickens, and Santa Rosa Areas the national seashore boundary extends on the north to the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and on the south one mile from the low tide line of the island. At Naval Live Oaks the national seashore boundary extends 100 yards from the low tide line.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 from the page DOM in the author's Chrome (accordion text present in DOM, not rendered by fetch tools). Whole page (about 152,000 characters) searched: zero matches for spear, projectile, Hawaiian, gig, bow/bows, '2.3'. Page carries 'Last updated: September 1, 2026' and no signature date. Park 'Fishing in Florida' page (www.nps.gov, last updated 28 Aug 2026): 'All fishing regulations for national seashore waters in Florida correspond with Florida fishing regulations.' and 'For more information regarding spear fishing regulations, please consult the Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission's website.' Stale pages still stating the ban: nps.gov/thingstodo/fishing-at-gulf-islands-national-seashore.htm (28 Feb 2022) and the home.nps.gov mirror of fishing-in-florida.htm (18 Mar 2021). 2021 source retained for history: https://www.nps.gov/guis/learn/news/national-seashore-releases-2021-superintendent-s-compendium.htm. 36 CFR 7.12 (Gulf Islands special regulations) has no fishing-gear or weapon provision (negative, eCFR as of 6 Oct 2026).

entries.cite: Canaveral National Seashore Superintendent's Compendium (last updated 12 Jun 2026), 36 CFR 1.5
entries.title: Canaveral NS: no boats operating or anchoring within 500 feet of the ocean beach
entries.effect: A dive boat may not operate or anchor within 500 feet of the ocean shoreline of the Seashore; beach-entry diving is not restricted by the compendium, and it contains no spearfishing rule.
entries.excerpt: Vessels may not operate or anchor within 500 feet (160 yards) of the mean low tide on any part of Canaveral National Seashore's ocean shoreline.
entries.scope: Ocean shoreline of Canaveral National Seashore (Apollo Beach to Playalinda Beach).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Two fetches returned the sentence with slightly different wording (one shortened), so marked secondary. Also: 'Crab fishing along beach road, vistas, and Eddy Creek is prohibited.' and 'Swimming is permitted within the boundaries of Canaveral National Seashore, except where closed by the posting of signs.' Confirmed negative: no spearfishing, spear or diving provision in the compendium. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.cite: Timucuan EHP, Castillo de San Marcos NM and Fort Matanzas NM compendia (2026)
entries.title: Northeast Florida NPS units: small shoreline fishing closures only
entries.effect: These three units close fishing only at named docks, boardwalks and historic frontages, and Fort Matanzas bans jumping, diving, snorkeling or swimming from its docks; none has a spearfishing rule.
entries.excerpt: Jumping, diving, snorkeling, or swimming from the Monument's docks is prohibited. [Fort Matanzas NM, 36 CFR 1.5]
entries.scope: Fort Matanzas NM (Matanzas Inlet, Rattlesnake Island); Castillo de San Marcos NM (St. Augustine bayfront); Timucuan EHP (Kingsley Plantation, Fort Caroline).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Fort Matanzas (approved 13 Jan 2026, updated 26 Mar 2026), 36 CFR 2.11: 'Fishing is prohibited from the shoreline above mean high tide between the Visitor Center dock gangway and posted NPS signage. Fishing is also prohibited from all other park boardwalks, docks, and from the shoreline above mean high tide within 50 feet of the fort dock gangway on Rattlesnake Island.' Castillo (same dates): 'Fishing is only permitted along the north green from north of the boardwalk to the end of the monument property.' and 'Jumping or diving from the seawall into the bay, the moat, or off the City Gates, Cubo Line and other historic structures is prohibited.' Timucuan (updated 3 Jun 2026): fishing prohibited at the Kingsley Plantation frontage, dock and retaining wall, and within Fort Caroline National Memorial. Low map value; could be a note rather than an entry. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.cite: 15 C.F.R. pt. 922 (all subparts); NOAA sanctuary nomination inventory: NEGATIVE
entries.title: No national marine sanctuary other than the Florida Keys touches Florida, and none is proposed
entries.effect: The Florida Keys NMS (subpart P) is the only sanctuary in Florida waters; no Florida or Gulf site is in NOAA's nomination inventory or in designation.
entries.excerpt: [No part 922 subpart other than subpart P (Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary) applies to Florida waters.]
entries.scope: Part 922 subparts F to W read 30 Sep 2026: Monitor, Channel Islands, Greater Farallones, Gray's Reef (off Georgia), American Samoa, Cordell Bank, Flower Garden Banks (off Texas and Louisiana), Monterey Bay, Stellwagen Bank, Olympic Coast, Florida Keys, Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale, Thunder Bay, Mallows Bay, Wisconsin Shipwreck Coast, Lake Ontario, Chumash Heritage, Papahānaumokuākea.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. NOAA nomination inventory (sanctuaries.noaa.gov/nominate/nominations.html): St. George Unangan Heritage (AK), Alaĝum Kanuux̂ (AK), Cashes Ledge Area (Gulf of Maine); 'Nominations Under Review by NOAA: None at this time.' In designation (sanctuaries.noaa.gov/management/designations.html): Hudson Canyon, Lake Erie Quadrangle, Pacific Islands Heritage. There is no Florida Middle Grounds sanctuary. Gray's Reef NMS off Sapelo Island, Georgia, is reachable from Jacksonville; its spearfishing rules were not read.

entries.cite: 50 C.F.R. pt. 622 subpart B (Gulf reef fish): NEGATIVE
entries.title: No federal Gulf rule on rebreathers or spearguns; the only Gulf spear rule is the stressed-area powerhead ban
entries.effect: In Gulf federal waters off Florida, spearguns and rebreathers are not restricted by any federal reef fish rule; only powerheads inside the stressed area and all fishing in the closed reserves are.
entries.excerpt: [No Gulf rebreather rule; no Gulf reef fish rule prohibiting spearfishing gear outside the closed areas of § 622.34 and § 622.74(b).]
entries.scope: Gulf EEZ off Florida.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. eCFR title 50 searches for 'rebreather' (only § 622.180, South Atlantic), 'powerhead' and 'spearfishing gear' in part 622, read 29 Sep 2026. § 622.32 bans only poisons; § 622.9 bans explosives 'except an explosive in a powerhead'. The Alabama SMZ (§ 622.35(d)) spearfishing text lies wholly off Alabama. Florida Middle Grounds HAPC has no diver, spear or anchoring rule.

entries.title: Kennedy Space Center security zone (launch days only)
entries.effect: Closed to all persons and vessels whenever a U.S. Government space launch from Cape Canaveral is scheduled; signalled by a red ball on 90-foot poles.
entries.excerpt: The area described in paragraph (a) of this section is closed to all vessels and persons, except those vessels and persons authorized by the Commander, USCG Southeast District, or the COTP Jacksonville, Florida, whenever space vehicles are to be launched by the United States Government from Cape Canaveral.
entries.scope: Mosquito Lagoon, Banana River north of the barge canal, Indian River at the NASA Causeway, and the Atlantic 3 miles offshore from the Haulover Canal south to the Port Canaveral channel. Boundary follows shorelines, a fence line, ICW edges and buoys; not drawable from the CFR.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Red balls on 90-foot poles at about 28°35′00″N 80°34′36″W and 28°25′18″N 80°35′00″W. COTP Jacksonville (904) 564-7513. Largely overlaps § 165.775 (launch RNA) and §§ 334.525, 334.570, 334.590, 334.595. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Tampa Bay area fixed security zones (Sector St. Petersburg)
entries.effect: Twelve fixed security zones around Tampa Bay port facilities, power plants and MacDill AFB, plus moving 500-yard and fixed 200-yard zones around cruise ships and hazardous-cargo vessels. Entry prohibited without COTP permission.
entries.excerpt: Entry into or remaining on or within the zones described in paragraph (a) of this section is prohibited unless authorized by the Captain of the Port St. Petersburg or a designated representative.
entries.full: Crystal River (ix) and Demory Gap (x) list four points in bow-tie order; the map draws them as channel strips (A-B-D-C).
entries.scope: Old Port Tampa; Sunshine Skyway main span (transit allowed, no loitering, anchoring or dive operations); Manbirtee Key 500 yards; Seaport Manatee; MacDill AFB; Port Sutton; Hooker's Point; St. Petersburg (Bayboro) Harbor; Crystal River nuclear plant channel and Demory Gap Channel; Big Bend; Weedon Island. Moving zones run from Egmont Channel buoys 9 and 10 to berth.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Rewritten by USCG-2025-0223, 90 FR 52563, 21 Nov 2025: the rewrite added Sunshine Skyway, Crystal River and Weedon Island zones and the dive-operation language. Sunshine Skyway (a)(1)(ii) verbatim: 'Any vessel may transit through this zone, but may not loiter, anchor, or conduct operations, including dredging, dive operation, surveying, or maintenance, unless otherwise directed by the Captain of the Port.' Fixed 200-yard zones around moored cruise ships (a)(2)(ii)(C): 'No vessel may loiter, anchor, or conduct maintenance operations within the security zone ... This includes, but is not limited to dredging operations, dive operations, and surveying.' Requests: WWMTampa@uscg.mil; Sector Command Center after hours 727.824.7506; changes broadcast on VHF 22A. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Port Canaveral East (Trident) and Middle Basin security zones
entries.effect: Entry, transit, anchoring or remaining in the Trident Basin (Zone A) or the Middle Basin (Zone B) is prohibited at all times without COTP Jacksonville permission.
entries.excerpt: All persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting through, anchoring in, or remaining within the security zone unless authorized by the COTP Jacksonville or a designated representative.
entries.scope: Zone A: all waters of the East Basin north of latitude 28°24′36″ N. Zone B: Middle Basin inside Points 1 to 7 then the land perimeter.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Permission: COTP Jacksonville 904-714-7557 or VHF 16. Overlaps § 334.600 (Trident Basin danger zone). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Port Everglades moving safety zone around naval aircraft carriers
entries.effect: Moving zone 700 yards ahead, 500 yards astern and 350 yards either side of an aircraft carrier from the Port Everglades sea buoy to its berth. No entry without COTP Miami permission.
entries.excerpt: No person or vessel may enter, transit, or remain in the safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port, Miami, Florida, or a Coast Guard commissioned, warrant, or petty officer designated by him.
entries.scope: Moving zone between the Port Everglades Sea Buoy (about 26°05.5′N 80°04.8′W) and the pier (about 26°04.9′N 80°06.9′W). List only; no fixed geometry.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). COTP Miami (305) 535-4472, VHF 16. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: St. Johns River fireworks safety zone, Jacksonville (Hart to Acosta bridges)
entries.effect: 500-yard zone around fireworks barges between the Hart and Acosta bridges, active when broadcast by the COTP until the display ends.
entries.excerpt: In accordance with the general regulations in 165.23 of this part, anchoring, mooring or transiting in this zone is prohibited unless authorized by the Captain of the Port or District Commander.
entries.scope: St. Johns River between the Hart and Acosta Bridges. Moving/temporary; list only.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Largely superseded in practice by the general fireworks section § 165.723. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: NAS Jacksonville security zone, St. Johns River
entries.effect: Water within about 400 feet of the NAS Jacksonville shoreline, from Timuquana Country Club south to the Buckman Bridge, is closed at all times without COTP permission.
entries.excerpt: In accordance with the general regulations in § 165.33 of this part, no person or vessel may enter or remain in the zone without the permission of the Captain of the Port Jacksonville, Florida.
entries.scope: St. Johns River, west bank at NAS Jacksonville: 30°14′39.5″N 81°40′45″W south to 30°11′42.30″N 81°41′23.66″W, 400 feet seaward of mean high water. Map shows corner markers only.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). COTP Jacksonville (904) 564-7513. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Fireworks safety zones, COTP Zone Jacksonville (500 yards)
entries.effect: 500-yard zone around any fireworks barge in the Jacksonville COTP zone during storage, preparation and launching. List only.
entries.excerpt: All persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting through, anchoring in, or remaining within the regulated area unless authorized by the Coast Guard Captain of the Port Jacksonville or a designated representative.
entries.scope: All waters of the Jacksonville COTP zone (roughly the Georgia line to about the Brevard/Indian River county area on the Atlantic side).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Notice by Broadcast Notice to Mariners or on-scene patrol. COTP Jacksonville (904) 564-7513. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Maritime Prepositioned Ship zones, St. Johns River and Blount Island
entries.effect: Zones around Maritime Prepositioned Ships: 200 yards while transiting the St. Johns River, 200 yards on the water at Blount Island Terminal, and the Gate Slip (Back River) while moored at Gate Terminal. Closed only while those ships are present.
entries.excerpt: The areas described in paragraph (a) of this section shall be closed to all vessels and persons, except those vessels and persons authorized by the Commander, USCG Southeast District or the Captain of the Port, Jacksonville, Florida, whenever specified Maritime Prepositioned Ships are transiting the St. Johns River (Zone A), moored at Blount Island (Zone B), or moored at Gate Terminal (Zone C).
entries.scope: Zone C closing line: 30°23′34″N 81°30′52″W to 30°23′38″N 81°30′36″W. Signal: rotating yellow light at Blount Island Marine Terminal or Gate Terminal Berth 1.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). § 165.728 (safety zones) and § 165.729 (security zones) are word-for-word twins. The § 165.729(b) wording was re-fetched and reads: 'The areas described in paragraph (a) of this section shall be closed to all vessels and persons, except those vessels and persons authorized by the Commander, USCG Southeast District or the Captain of the Port, Jacksonville, Florida, whenever specified Maritime Prepositioned Ships are transiting the St. Johns River (Zone A), moored at Blount Island (Zone B), or moored at Gate Terminal (Zone C).' Use that as the excerpt; the version above is the first, summarised return. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Kings Bay submarine base zones, Cumberland Sound and St. Marys entrance (Georgia side, reaches Florida waters)
entries.effect: Permanent security zone off Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay (Georgia), a slow-speed RNA in Kings Bay, and a 1 nm RNA around escorted submarines and along the St. Marys Entrance Channel, which borders Fernandina Beach and Fort Clinch.
entries.excerpt: All persons and vessels located within a RNA created by paragraph (a) shall follow all lawful orders and/or directions given to them by designated Coast Guard representatives.
entries.scope: § 165.732(a)(2): all waters within 1 nm of the channel centre from Crab Island to lighted buoy STM, whenever a submarine is under Coast Guard escort. The § 165.731 fixed security zone and the § 165.730 speed RNA are in Georgia waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Include only as a list item for the Fernandina Beach / Fort Clinch jetties area. Georgia fixed-zone coordinates were read but not mapped. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Jacksonville, Fernandina and Canaveral: 100-yard zones around tankers, cruise ships and prepositioned ships
entries.effect: Moving 100-yard zones around tank vessels, cruise ships and military prepositioned ships entering or leaving port, and fixed 100-yard zones around them while docked.
entries.excerpt: In accordance with the general regulations § 165.33 of this part, entry into these zones is prohibited except as authorized by the Captain of the Port, or a Coast Guard commissioned, warrant, or petty officer designated by him.
entries.scope: Activation points: St. Johns River Sea Buoy (about 30°23′35″N 81°19′08″W); Port Canaveral Channel Entrance Buoys 3 and 4. Moving and vessel-relative; list only.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Status changes broadcast on VHF 22 (157.1 MHz). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Palm Beach, Port Everglades and Miami: vessel zones and fixed port security zones
entries.effect: Moving and fixed 100-yard zones around passenger, hazardous-cargo and LHG vessels in all three ports; a fixed zone in Miami Main Channel; and fixed zones west of the ICW at Port Everglades from Mid-Port to North-Port and south to the Dania Cut-Off Canal.
entries.excerpt: In accordance with the general regulations § 165.33, entry into these zones is prohibited, except as authorized by the Captain of the Port of Miami or a designated representative.
entries.scope: Moving zones activate at Lake Worth Lighted Buoy LW (26°46′22″N 80°00′37″W), Port Everglades Lighted Buoy PE (26°05′30″N 80°04′46″W) and Miami Lighted Buoy M (25°46′05″N 80°05′01″W). Miami Main Channel fixed zone and Port Everglades fixed zones have CFR coordinates.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Replaces the part of existing entry cfr-33-165-760 that describes § 165.760 alone. Last amended by USCG-2022-0058, 89 FR 105456, 27 Dec 2024. COTP Miami (305) 535-4472, VHF 16. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Port of Key West: 100-yard zones around cruise ships and hazardous-cargo vessels
entries.effect: Moving 100-yard zones around passenger, hazardous-cargo and LHG vessels from Key West Entrance Buoy KW inbound, and fixed 100-yard zones while moored.
entries.excerpt: In accordance with the general regulations § 165.33, entry into these zones is prohibited except as authorized by the Captain of the Port of Key West or a designated representative.
entries.scope: Activation at Key West Entrance Lighted Whistle Buoy KW, about 24°27′26″N 81°48′00″W. Vessel-relative; list only.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). COTP Key West (305) 292-8727, VHF 16. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Coast Guard Sector Key West security zone, Trumbo Point (no anchoring, loitering or fishing)
entries.effect: All waters within 100 yards of Sector Key West. No entry without COTP permission, except transit at safe speed through Fleming Key Cut and Key West Bight Channel; anchoring, loitering and fishing prohibited.
entries.excerpt: While anchoring, loitering, or fishing activities are prohibited, vessels may transit the following portions of the security zone at safe speed:
entries.scope: Anchor points 24°34′02″N 81°47′52.7″W; 24°33′50.6″N 81°48′11.0″W; 24°33′48.8″N 81°47′54.8″W; 100-yard offsets follow the property line.

entries.title: Port Everglades harbor RNA: slow speed only, NOT an entry or diving ban
entries.effect: Vessels under 150 m must proceed at slow speed through the Bar Cut / Lake Mabel area. No entry, anchoring or diving restriction.
entries.excerpt: Vessels less than 150 meters entering and transiting through the regulated navigation area shall proceed at a slow speed.
entries.scope: Bar Cut and Lake Mabel, Port Everglades; four CFR points.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Speed rule only. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Escorted vessels, COTP Zone Jacksonville: 500-yard moving security zone
entries.effect: 500-yard zone around any vessel under law-enforcement escort anywhere in the Jacksonville COTP zone; nobody may enter the inner 100 yards.
entries.excerpt: No vessel or person may enter the inner 100-yard portion of the security zone closest to the vessel.
entries.scope: All navigable waters of COTP Zone Jacksonville. Vessel-relative; list only.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Permission to enter the outer 400 yards may be requested; then minimum safe speed. COTP Jacksonville (904) 564-7513, VHF 16. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Cape Canaveral launch RNA and five launch hazard areas
entries.effect: Before and just after a launch, the COTP may close any of five prescribed launch hazard areas, or ad hoc areas, anywhere between about 28°11′N and 28°49′N out to 12 nm.
entries.excerpt: The COTP Jacksonville or a designated representative may restrict vessel movement including but not limited to transiting, anchoring, or mooring within this RNA to protect vessels from hazards associated with rocket launches.
entries.scope: RNA: 28°48′54″N 80°28′40″W to 28°43′20″N 80°41′00″W, along shore to 28°25′18″N 80°34′43″W, to 28°11′00″N 80°29′00″W, to 28°10′00″N 80°21′13″W, then the 12 nm line (WGS 84). Five launch hazard areas have full CFR point lists.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). (c)(1) continues verbatim: 'These restrictions are temporary in nature and will only be enacted and enforced prior to and just after a launch.' Notice by Broadcast Notice to Mariners on VHF 16, Public Notice of Enforcement, and yellow balls on 90-foot poles. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Port Canaveral West Basin cruise ship security zone
entries.effect: West Basin northwest of the CFR line is closed from 4 hours before a cruise ship arrives until all cruise ships leave, but only at MARSEC 2 or 3 (or a specific threat at MARSEC 1).
entries.excerpt: Under general security zone regulations of 33 CFR 165.33, no vessel or person may enter or navigate within the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Red ball on a 50-foot pole at the east end of Cruise Terminal 10. COTP (904) 564-7513. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Biscayne Bay holiday events RNA: 15-knot limit only
entries.effect: 15-knot speed limit and Coast Guard control in central and south Biscayne Bay on Columbus Day weekend, New Year's Eve night and Fourth of July fireworks night. No entry ban.
entries.excerpt: All vessels within the regulated area are required to transit at no more than 15 knots, are subject to control by the Coast Guard, and must follow the instructions of designated representatives.
entries.scope: Biscayne Bay from Julia Tuttle Causeway to Turkey Point; seven CFR points.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). Speed rule only. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Fireworks safety zones, COTP Zone St. Petersburg (500 yards)
entries.effect: 500-yard zone around any fireworks platform, structure or barge in the St. Petersburg COTP zone during storage, preparation and launch. List only.
entries.excerpt: All persons and vessels are prohibited from entering, transiting through, anchoring in, or remaining within the regulated area unless authorized by the Coast Guard Captain of the Port St. Petersburg or a designated representative.
entries.scope: All waters of the Sector St. Petersburg COTP zone (Gulf coast from about Chokoloskee to the Wakulla/Jefferson line).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 on eCFR (page shows up to date as of 24 Sep 2026). entries.effect: Enforced when the President, First Family or other Secret Service protectees are at or expected at Mar-a-Lago.
entries.excerpt: This section will be enforced when the President of the United States, members of the First Family, or other persons under the protection of the Secret Service are present or expected to be present at the Mar-a-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.

entries.title: Biscayne Bay-Card Sound Spiny Lobster Sanctuary: no lobster, ever, and no lobster aboard while anyone is in the water
entries.effect: Year-round, nobody may take or disturb spiny lobster anywhere in Biscayne Bay, Card Sound and Little Card Sound west of the keys, and a boat with lobster aboard may not have anyone overboard inside the sanctuary.
entries.excerpt: It is unlawful for any person to molest, take or trap any spiny lobster, for any purpose, within the boundaries of the sanctuary, unless such person holds a special permit issued by the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.
entries.full: r. 68B-11.001(1): "The waters of Biscayne Bay, Card Sound, and Little Card Sound hereinafter described are declared to be a nursery sanctuary for the purpose of protecting the spiny lobster." Boundary begins "at the intersection of the northern right-of-way of State Road 905A and the western mean high water line of Little Card Sound", runs north along the mainland shore to the canal at the northern boundary of Matheson Hammock Park, then by straight lines and eastern mean high water lines to Cape Florida, Soldier Key, the Ragged Keys, Boca Chita, Sands, Elliott, Old Rhodes, Swan, Palo Alto and Angelfish Keys and Key Largo, closing along SR 905A. "The western boundary of the sanctuary from the point of beginning to the northern boundary of Matheson Hammock Park, includes all natural and artificial waterways tidally connected to Little Card Sound, Card Sound, and Biscayne Bay." r. 68B-11.004: "The presence of spiny lobster aboard a vessel within the boundaries of the sanctuary, while one or more persons from such vessel are overboard, is prohibited and constitutes a violation of this chapter by all persons aboard and overboard from such vessel", with exceptions for passage and temporary safe refuge while nobody is overboard. Penalty: second-degree misdemeanour (r. 68B-11.003).
entries.scope: Biscayne Bay south of a line from the Matheson Hammock Park canal to Cape Florida, Card Sound and Little Card Sound, west of the keys, plus every tidally connected mainland waterway. Boundary is WORDS ONLY (mean high water lines, headland-to-headland lines, one section-township-range tie point); the rule gives no coordinates, so no geometry is produced here. FWC publishes a digitised polygon: gis.myfwc.com Open_Data/Spiny_Lobster_Sanctuary_Biscayne_Bay_Florida/MapServer/6.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: NEW. Lobster-only; spearfishing for finfish is unaffected. It overlaps the west half of Biscayne National Park (drawn as open). The 68B-11.004 rule bites a diver who carries lobster from outside onto a boat that then stops inside the sanctuary for a dive. Rules dated 1984 and 1996, never amended since. entries.cite: Fla. Admin. Code r. 68B-24.0065 (as amended eff. 1 Jul 2026)
entries.title: John Pennekamp: no lobster in the sport season; seven Coral Formation Protection Zones closed to lobster all regular season
entries.effect: In John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park nobody may take lobster during the two-day sport season, and during the regular season lobster harvest and traps are banned in seven buoyed Coral Formation Protection Zones and on any patch reef.
entries.excerpt: (1) During the two-day sport season established in subsection 68B-24.005(2), F.A.C., there shall be no harvest of spiny lobster in John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park. Except for persons transiting park waters in a vessel, no person shall possess any spiny lobster in or on the waters of the park during this period. Possession of spiny lobster during this period aboard any vessel from which a person is diving, within the boundaries of the park, is prohibited.
entries.full: (2)(a): during the regular season "no person shall harvest or attempt to harvest any species of the Genera Panulirus or Scyllarides, or deploy any trap, in the following described areas of John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, each of which is a polygon bounded by the lines connecting the coordinates as expressed by latitude and longitude". (2)(b) no possession in those areas; (2)(c) no lobster harvest or traps "from or within any patch reef", defined as "any coral formation, consisting of a roughly circular area of hard corals, soft corals, and a mixture of other benthic invertebrates." The 1 Jul 2026 amendment replaced the ten 1995 zones with seven: Turtle Rocks, Basin Hill, Higdon's Reef, Cannon Patch, Mosquito Bank N., Mosquito Bank S.E., Three Sisters (geometry.json, ids penncpz-*). entries.title: Western Dry Rocks: no fishing of any kind, 1 April to 31 July
entries.effect: Every spring, 1 April through 31 July, all fishing including spearfishing, and possession of fish, is prohibited in the state waters of a box at Western Dry Rocks off Key West; the rule sunsets after 31 March 2028 unless renewed.
entries.excerpt: Fishing and possession of fish are prohibited within Western Dry Rocks, described in subsection (1), from April 1 through July 31. However, fish may be possessed aboard a vessel, provided such vessel is in continuous transit through Western Dry Rocks, fishing gear is appropriately stowed, and such resources are stowed in a cabin, locker, or similar storage area prior to entering and during transit through Western Dry Rocks. For the purpose of this subsection, appropriately stowed means hooks cannot be baited, and spear shafts shall not be inserted into any spearing device. All hook-and-line gear, spearing equipment, nets, and other harvesting equipment must be secured in a manner that makes their immediate use impracticable. This closure shall only remain in effect through March 31, 2028. However, the Commission shall review the closure prior to that date and determine whether repeal is appropriate or if the closure should be renewed or expanded.

entries.title: Coral Reef Protection Act: anchoring on reef is penalised; NOT a fishing rule
entries.effect: Anchoring on or grounding on coral or colonised hard bottom off Martin, Palm Beach, Broward, Miami-Dade and Monroe counties carries civil penalties from $225 (a first warning letter for a registered recreational boat) up to $375,000; it does not restrict fishing or spearfishing.
entries.excerpt: (2) This act applies to the sovereign submerged lands that contain coral reefs as defined in this act off the coasts of Broward, Martin, Miami-Dade, Monroe, and Palm Beach Counties. ... (8)(a) For any anchoring of a vessel on a coral reef or for any other damage to a coral reef totaling less than or equal to an area of 1 square meter, $225, provided that a responsible party who has anchored a recreational vessel as defined in s. 327.02 which is lawfully registered or exempt from registration pursuant to chapter 328 is issued, at least once, a warning letter in lieu of penalty; with aggravating circumstances, an additional $225; occurring within a state park or aquatic preserve, an additional $225.
entries.full: (3)(c) "Coral reefs" means "Limestone structures composed wholly or partially of living corals, their skeletal remains, or both, and hosting other coral, associated benthic invertebrates, and plants" or "Hard-bottom communities, also known as live bottom habitat or colonized pavement, characterized by the presence of coral and associated reef organisms or worm reefs created by the Phragmatopoma species." (5): the responsible party "must notify the department of such an event within 24 hours" and remove the vessel "within 72 hours". Higher bands: 1 to 10 m2 $450 per m2; over 10 m2 $1,500 per m2; repeat violations doubled, tripled, quadrupled; cap $375,000 per occurrence. History: s. 57, ch. 2009-86; s. 86, ch. 2010-5; s. 76, ch. 2015-229; s. 24, ch. 2020-158.
entries.scope: Sovereign submerged lands containing coral reefs off Broward, Martin, Miami-Dade, Monroe and Palm Beach Counties. The definition includes colonised pavement and Phragmatopoma worm reef, so it reaches nearshore hard bottom, not only coral reef.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: NEW. Popup and sidebar material, not a closure. entries.title: Discharge of air, gas or spring-powered projectile weapons banned citywide, spearfishing excepted only where designated
entries.effect: Firing any spring, gas or mechanically powered projectile weapon is unlawful anywhere in the city; the only spearfishing exception is 'in any area where such activity has been designated as permissible' by the city, state or federal government.

entries.title: Spear fishing prohibited within or near city waters
entries.effect: Spearfishing of any kind (hand spear, sling, band or pneumatic gun) is unlawful within or near the territorial waters of the City of Venice.
entries.excerpt:
(a) Definition. As used in this section, the term "spear fishing" means the taking or attempted taking of fish or other marine life from the territorial waters of the city by discharging, throwing, casting or hurling any spear, rod, arrow or other projectile for the purpose of spearing, piercing or impaling fish or other marine life, whether the projectile be propelled or manipulated by hand or by any airgun, spring gun or other contrivance, except that it shall not include the bringing of such game to gaff after being taken by ordinary methods of angling or netting, or the killing from the surface of dangerous marine life for the purpose of avoiding a public hazard, or the gigging of fish from the surface.

(b) Prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to engage or attempt to engage in spear fishing within or near the territorial waters of the city.
entries.full: History note: (Code 1982, § 13-48). Chapter 46 art. IV div. 2 (Fishing and swimming). Division 3 (Skin and scuba diving) adds: § 46-132 diver's flag within 100 ft; § 46-134 no skin or scuba diving in any marked navigable channel unless authorized by the police department; § 46-135 no skin or scuba diving within 200 ft of any person fishing or any anchored boat. § 46-64: no diving from the Venice Fishing Pier or swimming within 150 ft of its centerline.
entries.scope: 'Within or near the territorial waters of the city.' The city's territorial waters are not defined in the section. The Venice city limits include Gulf beaches from about Venice Inlet south past the Venice Fishing Pier and Caspersen Beach, and the Venice Inlet jetties. 'Near' has no stated distance.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. NEW and HIGH IMPACT. This is the only Gulf-coast city ordinance found that bans spearfishing outright across the whole city waterfront, including the Venice beach ledges and fossil-tooth dive sites. Conservative reading: treat all Gulf water off the Venice city limits out to the 9 nm state line as 'near', and the Venice Inlet and ICW within city limits as closed; at minimum draw the city limits extended seaward. Preemption: this regulates the taking of saltwater fish by name, the same § 379.2425 question as Treasure Island; untested, plan around it. Code current through Ord. No. 2026-19 (26 May 2026), Supp. No. 86 Update 1. entries.title: City of Sarasota: spear fishing banned within 100 yards of city docks, bridges, piers, wharves and jetties at beaches and recreational areas; channel and flag rules
entries.effect: Inside the City of Sarasota, no spearfishing within 100 yards of any city dock, bridge, pier, wharf or jetty at a recreational area or public bathing beach, and no skin diving, scuba or spearfishing in marked channels or within 200 ft of anglers or anchored boats.
entries.excerpt:
Sec. 10-66. It shall be unlawful for any person to spear fish within a recreational area or public or municipal bathing beach within one hundred (100) yards of any dock, bridge, pier, wharf or jetty of the city.

Sec. 10-64. It shall be unlawful for any person to skin dive, scuba dive or spear fish within the bounds of any marked navigable channel unless permission is obtained from the appropriate law enforcement agency by the showing of some necessity for diving in such channel.

Sec. 10-65. It shall be unlawful for any person to skin dive, scuba dive or spear fish within two hundred (200) feet of any person fishing, or any boat anchored, prior to commencement of diving or spear fishing. There shall be excluded from the operation of this section any boat from which a diver is skin diving, scuba diving or spear fishing.
entries.full: Sec. 10-62. History notes: § 10-62 (Code 1971, § 11-17); § 10-64 (Code 1971, § 11-19); § 10-65 (Code 1971, § 11-20); § 10-66 (Code 1971, § 11-21). Ch. 10 art. entries.title: No harpoons or spears from Dunedin Marina docks and seawalls; posted no-fishing areas include spears
entries.effect: No spear or harpoon use from the Dunedin Marina docks, walkways and seawalls, and no swimming in the marina; posted city no-fishing areas bar spears too.
entries.excerpt: No bicycling or roller skating shall be allowed on the boardwalks of the marina. No cast netting or other fishing, or the use of harpoons or spears, is allowed from the docks, walkways and seawalls within the Dunedin Marina. entries.title: Fishing (defined to include spearing) prohibited at eight listed city shorelines and waters; no propelling spears in city park areas
entries.effect: In Fort Pierce, spearing counts as fishing, and fishing is banned at eight listed places, two of them expressly 'in, on, upon or under the waters' (Moore's Creek and the city marina); separately, propelling a spear in any city park area, which includes waterways, canals and beaches, is unlawful.
entries.excerpt: (a) The city hereby prohibits fishing from certain specified areas, as follows: ... (3) From the land or shoreline, in, on, upon or under the waters of Moore's Creek, east of Indian River Drive, being the area where Moore's Creek enters the Indian River Lagoon; (4) From the land or shoreline, including structures attached thereto, in, on, upon or under the waters of the city marina, except as otherwise provided by marina rules or dockage license agreements; ... (c) Areas encompassed and included in this section, wherein fishing is prohibited, shall be posted with signage indicating such restriction. [§ 28-31(18)] To launch, throw, hurl, or otherwise propel an arrow, spear, BB, pellet, slingshot, or other dangerous object, except that in accordance with F.S. § 790.33, this subsection (18) shall not be used to regulate firearms, ammunition, or components thereof, as defined in F.S. ch. 790;
entries.full: § 28-1 'Fishing': 'taking or attempting to take, possess, remove, or capture fish or other marine life, by means of any type of pole, rod, net, spear gun, spear, lance, gig, or any type of device used for taking, removing, possessing, or capturing fish'. § 28-1 'Park area': 'all parks, playgrounds, recreation fields and areas, waterways, water areas, canals, beaches, buildings, structures and facilities ... within the city limits, excluding state and federal parks'. § 28-4 other areas: South Bridge on Seaway Drive (except the walkways beneath); River Walk; Marina Square; Inlet Linear Park sidewalk (not the South Jetty); Jaycee Park; S. Causeway Park (to just west of the concrete pier). History § 28-4: (Code 1983, § 12-103; Ord. No. L-246, § 2, 2-21-2012; Ord. No. 24-014, § 1, 5-20-2024). § 28-31: (Code 1983, § 12-202; ...; Ord. No. 24-014, § 4, 5-20-2024). § 28-35 Surfside Park: no surf fishing.
entries.scope: Fort Pierce: Moore's Creek mouth, city marina waters, and six shore locations; all city park areas including waterways and beaches for the § 28-31(18) spear clause.
entries.note: Re-read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com (Supplement 20, 2 Feb 2026); each section came back whole, so upgraded to verbatim. § 28-4(b): the no-fishing areas are shown on a diagram on file with the city clerk; (c): they are posted. Items (1), (2), (5) to (8) are 'from' land or structures (shore fishing); (3) and (4) reach the water. 'Park area' may be limited by 'provided in connection therewith'; conservative reading keeps all city waterways, canals and beaches. entries.title: Swimming, diving and fishing forbidden in the Lake Park Harbor Marina
entries.effect: No swimming, diving or fishing inside Lake Park Harbor Marina (limited angling and small cast nets excepted).
entries.excerpt: Swimming, diving and fishing are forbidden within the marina area; provided, however, that persons may fish and may use cast nets measuring eight feet or less stretched length (stretched length is defined as the distance from the horn at the center of the net with the net gathered and pulled taut, to the lead line) within designated areas located along the marina bulkhead into the Lake Worth Lagoon, east of the established bulkhead line from sunrise to sunset.
entries.scope: Lake Park Harbor Marina, Lake Worth Lagoon.
entries.note: Read whole 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com (Supplement 57, 17 Jun 2026). The exception lets people fish from designated bulkhead areas only; diving is forbidden outright, so the marina basin is closed to divers.

entries.title: Reef fish minimum sizes (snapper, grouper, hogfish, amberjacks, triggerfish, sea bass, red porgy)
entries.effect: Sets the state minimum size for each reef fish, in total length for snappers, groupers, black sea bass and red porgy, and fork length for amberjacks, gray triggerfish and hogfish.
entries.excerpt: No person shall land, possess, unnecessarily destroy, purchase, exchange, sell or offer for sale any of the following species harvested in or from state waters, of a length less than set forth as follows:
entries.full: Values read from the 26 Oct 2023 text (summarised list, not quoted): gag and black grouper 24 in TL; red, yellowfin, yellowmouth grouper 20 in TL; scamp 20 in TL Atlantic and Monroe, 16 in TL Gulf; goliath 24 to 36 in TL; hogfish 16 in FL Atlantic and south of 25 deg 09 min N, 14 in FL north; greater amberjack 28 in FL Atlantic, 34 in FL Gulf (recreational); banded rudderfish and lesser amberjack 14 to 22 in FL; gray triggerfish 12 in FL Atlantic, 15 in FL Gulf (recreational); black sea bass 13 in TL Atlantic (recreational), 10 in TL Gulf; red porgy 14 in TL Atlantic; snappers in TL: cubera 12, dog 12, gray 10 (recreational), lane 8, mahogany 12, mutton 18, red 20 Atlantic and 16 Gulf (recreational), schoolmaster 10, vermilion 12 Atlantic and 10 Gulf, yellowtail 12. The 1 Apr 2026 amendment raised Gulf state-water lane snapper to 10 in TL (FAR notice 30105616; FWC).
entries.scope: State waters, Atlantic and Gulf.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: the version in force is effective 1 Apr 2026 (flrules notice 30630483). Cornell LII and Justia (current through 24 Jun 2025) both carry the 26 Oct 2023 text.
