entries.title: Reef fish bag and vessel limits; Atlantic and Keys gag and black grouper: 1 per person and 2 per vessel combined from 28 Oct 2026
entries.effect: Snapper aggregate 10 per person. Grouper aggregate 4 per person in the Gulf outside Monroe County, 3 in the Atlantic and all Monroe County waters. From 28 Oct 2026, in Atlantic and all Monroe County state waters, 1 gag or black grouper per person per day and no more than 2 gag or black grouper in any combination aboard any vessel at any time. Gulf state waters outside Monroe: no more than 2 gag per person within the aggregate.
entries.excerpt: (1)(a) ... no recreational harvester shall harvest within or without Florida waters, nor possess within or without Florida waters, more than a total of 10 snapper per day, in any combination of species. ... (2)(b)1. No recreational harvester shall harvest in or from all Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County, nor possess while in or on Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County, more than 1 gag or black grouper per day and no more than 2 gag or black grouper in any combination shall be possessed aboard any vessel in or on Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County at any time (consistent with Federal Standard established in 50 C.F.R §622.187 as of October 28, 2026).
entries.full: Other limits read (2024 text): gray snapper 5 in state waters; red snapper 2 (Atlantic and Gulf); vermilion 5 Atlantic, 10 Gulf, outside aggregate; Gulf lane snapper outside aggregate; cubera 30 in TL or larger 2 per person and 2 per vessel, outside aggregate; mutton 5; 1 gag or black in Atlantic and Monroe; 2 gag and 2 red grouper in Gulf (excluding Monroe); Gulf for-hire captain and crew 0 for gag, red, black; speckled hind and warsaw 1 each per person and per vessel; snowy 1 per person and per vessel Atlantic and Monroe; goliath 1 per permit holder per season; hogfish 1 (Atlantic and south of 25 deg 09 min N), 5 north; black sea bass 7 Atlantic; red porgy 1 Atlantic; greater amberjack 1; banded rudderfish and lesser amberjack 5 combined; golden tilefish 1 Atlantic; blueline tilefish 2 Atlantic and Monroe; gray triggerfish 1 Gulf, 10 Atlantic.
entries.scope: State waters; aggregate limits apply 'within or without Florida waters'.
entries.note: UPDATED 11 Nov 2026. FLRules shows a new final adopted version, rule file date 26 Oct 2026, effective 28 Oct 2026 (notice 31547424, adopting the 5 Oct 2026 proposal, notice 31448290). The adopted .doc (tid 31547424) was fetched in the author's Chrome from flrules.org and its text extracted in the page; (1)(a) and (2)(b)1. are quoted from that text, whitespace collapsed. The page title reads 'Recreational Bag and Vessel Limits'; the first line of the .doc reads 'Recreational Bag Limits'. The state vessel limit has no charter exception: 2 gag or black grouper combined aboard any vessel at any time, which is stricter than the federal for-hire limit of 2 per trip. Earlier notes said the text in force since 1 Apr 2026 had not been read; that version is superseded.

entries.title: Gulf red snapper season: set each year by FWC notice
entries.effect: Gulf red snapper is closed in state waters except during the open season FWC announces on its snapper page; there is no fixed season in the rule. The rule does not cover the Atlantic.
entries.excerpt: (1) Red Snapper Open Seasons. Pursuant to Section 120.81(5), F.S., the Commission shall give notice of red snapper open seasons for all waters of the Gulf of Mexico: electronically at: www.myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/snappers/. (2) Red Snapper Closed Seasons. Except as provided elsewhere in this chapter, no recreational harvester shall harvest in or from state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, nor possess while in or on state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, any red snapper outside of the open season established by the procedure in subsection (1).
entries.scope: Gulf state waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 5 May 2024, matches flrules. 2026 Gulf dates: see fwc-rs-gulf-2026. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Goliath grouper open and closed harvest areas
entries.effect: Permit harvest of goliath (hook and line only) is closed from Martin through Miami-Dade, the Atlantic side of Monroe, Dry Tortugas NP and the St. Lucie River.
entries.excerpt: All Florida Waters of Martin through Miami-Dade counties, all Florida Waters of the Atlantic Ocean in Monroe County, all Florida Waters within Dry Tortugas National Park, and all Florida Waters of the St. Lucie River and its tributaries.
entries.full: Open: 'all Florida Waters of Nassau through St. Lucie counties, all Florida Waters of the Gulf of Mexico in Monroe County, and all Florida Waters of Collier through Escambia counties', less the closed areas.
entries.scope: Florida Waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Jul 2022 matches flrules. Excerpt is the closed-area list; subsection numbers not captured. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Cobia: 36 in fork length, 1 per person, 2 per vessel
entries.effect: Cobia must be 36 in fork length; 1 per person per day and 2 per vessel. Chapter 68B-19 has no gear rule, so it does not exclude spear as gear.
entries.excerpt: [68B-19.003(1):] A person may not harvest or land from Florida Waters, or possess in or on Florida Waters, a cobia that is less than 36 inches in fork length. [68B-19.004(1)(a):] A recreational harvester may not harvest or land from Florida Waters, or possess in or on Florida Waters, more than 1 cobia per day. [(1)(b):] The recreational harvesters aboard a vessel in or on Florida Waters may not collectively possess or land more than 2 cobia, regardless of the number of persons onboard.
entries.scope: Florida Waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: flrules shows both rules effective 5 Jul 2022; Justia's history says 7-1-22. Minor date discrepancy, not resolved. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Sheepshead: 12 in TL, 8 per person; spear not excluded as gear
entries.effect: Sheepshead 12 in total length, 8 per person per day, 50 per vessel in March and April; spearing is a listed gear. Applies within or without Florida Waters.
entries.excerpt: [.003] A person may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land, a sheepshead that is less than 12 inches in total length. [.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land more than 8 sheepshead per day. ... During the months of March and April, no more than 50 sheepshead may be collectively possessed by recreational harvesters aboard a vessel within or without Florida Waters, regardless of the number of persons onboard. [.006] A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a sheepshead within or without Florida Waters only by or with the use of beach or haul seine, cast net, hook and line gear, or by spearing.
entries.scope: State and federal waters ('within or without Florida Waters').
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: all three rules 1 Jul 2018, match flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Flounder: 14 in TL, 5 per person, closed Oct 15 to Nov 30; spear not excluded as gear
entries.effect: Flounder 14 in total length, 5 per person per day, closed every year Oct 15 to Nov 30; spearing is a listed gear. Applies within or without Florida Waters.
entries.excerpt: [.003(1)] A person may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land a flounder that is less than 14 inches in total length. [.004(1)] A recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land more than 5 flounder per day. [.005(1)] A recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land a flounder beginning October 15 and continuing through November 30 each year. [.006(1)] A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a flounder within or without Florida Waters only by or with the use of beach or haul seine, cast net, hook and line gear, or by spearing.
entries.scope: State and federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: all four rules 1 Mar 2021, match flrules. 2026 closure: Oct 15 to Nov 30, 2026. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Black drum: 14 to 24 in TL slot, 5 per person; no spear ban
entries.effect: Black drum slot 14 to 24 in total length with one over 24 in per person, 5 per person. The gear rule bans multiple hooks with natural bait and snagging only, so it does not exclude spear as gear.
entries.excerpt: [.003] ... a recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land a black drum that is less than 14 inches or greater than 24 inches in total length. [.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest within or without Florida Waters or land per day more than 5 black drum or possess within or without Florida Waters more than 5 black drum. [.006(2)] A person may not harvest or attempt to harvest a black drum within or without Florida Waters by snagging the black drum or land a black drum so harvested.
entries.full: The one-fish-over-24-in allowance is in .003 (summarised). .006(1) bars a multiple hook with natural bait.
entries.scope: State and federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: all 1 Sep 2013, match flrules. Confirmed negative: no spear prohibition in ch. 68B-36 (all six rules listed; .003, .004, .006 read). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Tripletail: hook and line only; spearing prohibited in state and federal waters
entries.effect: Tripletail may be taken only by hook and line, anywhere, including federal waters. This is a second, independent spearing ban alongside r. 68B-20.005(17).
entries.excerpt: A person may harvest a tripletail within or without Florida Waters only by or with the use of hook and line gear. ... A person may not harvest within or without Florida Waters a tripletail by spearing or snagging the tripletail.
entries.scope: State and federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Jul 2018 matches flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Sharks: hook and line only
entries.effect: Sharks may be taken from Florida Waters only with hook and line. With r. 68B-20.005(10), spearing any shark is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a shark from Florida Waters only by or with the use of hook-and-line gear.
entries.scope: Florida Waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Jul 2019 matches flrules. R. 68B-44.004 amended 12 Jan 2026 (Carolina hammerhead made prohibited); not relevant to spear status. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Spiny lobster: no device that can puncture or crush
entries.effect: No spear, hook or other device that could puncture or crush a lobster may be used. Spiny lobster cannot be speared.
entries.excerpt: No person shall harvest or attempt to harvest spiny lobster using any device which will or could puncture, penetrate, or crush the exoskeleton (shell) or the flesh of the lobster, and the use of such devices as part of, or in conjunction with, any trap is also prohibited.
entries.scope: State waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 May 2017 matches flrules. This, not r. 68B-20.005, is the lobster spearing ban. R. 68B-24.0065 (Pennekamp) amended 1 Jul 2026, not read. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Lionfish: no bag limit; licence exemption for spears and nets; rebreather ban exception
entries.effect: Lionfish have no bag or size limit. A diver using a hand net, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or lionfish-specific spear is exempt from the licence requirement. The rebreather harvest ban does not apply to lionfish.
entries.excerpt: (2) A recreational fishing license is not required for harvesting lionfish by divers only if using the following gear: (a) Hand held net; (b) Pole spear; (c) Hawaiian sling, or (d) Any other spearing device specifically designed and exclusively marketed towards lionfish. (3) Lionfish shall have no commercial or recreational bag limit. ... (4) The harvest of lionfish while using a rebreather is allowed in accordance with subsection 68B-4.012(2), F.A.C.
entries.scope: State waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 26 Nov 2014 matches flrules. A speargun (trigger device) is not on the licence-exempt list; a licence is needed for it. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Great barracuda: slot and 2 per person from Martin and Collier counties south
entries.effect: Off Collier, Monroe, Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach and Martin, in state and adjacent federal waters: 15 to 36 in fork length, one over 36 in, 2 per person, 6 per vessel. No gear rule.
entries.excerpt: [.003] ... a person may not harvest or land a great barracuda from the above described region or possess in or on the waters of the described region a great barracuda that is less than 15 inches in fork length or greater than 36 inches in fork length. [.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest, possess, or land more than two great barracuda per day ...
entries.full: Region (.003 chapeau): state and adjacent federal waters of the Gulf south of a line due west from the Collier-Lee County line (26 deg 19.823 min N) and of the Atlantic south of a line due east from the Martin-St. Lucie County line (27 deg 15.781 min N). Vessel limit six per day. North of those lines FWC applies the 2 fish or 100 lb default.
entries.scope: Southern region, state and adjacent federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: .003 1 Jan 2017 and .004 1 Nov 2015 match flrules. Confirmed negative: no gear rule in ch. 68B-60 (three rules). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Wahoo: 2 per person
entries.effect: Wahoo limit is 2 per person per day, no size limit. Chapter 68B-57 has no gear rule.
entries.excerpt: A recreational harvester may not harvest or land per day from Florida Waters or possess in or on Florida Waters more than 2 wahoo.
entries.scope: Florida Waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Sep 2013 matches flrules. Confirmed negative: no gear rule among the six ch. 68B-57 rules (titles checked). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Dolphin: bag and vessel limits; spear not excluded as gear
entries.effect: Dolphin 10 per person and 60 per vessel in the Gulf, 5 per person and 30 per vessel in the Atlantic. The rule lists hook and line and spearing as gear, within or without Florida waters.
entries.excerpt: [.004, Gulf] A recreational harvester may not harvest or land per day from Florida Waters or possess in or on Florida Waters more than 10 dolphin. [.004, Atlantic] ... more than 5 dolphin. [.006] A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a dolphin within or without Florida Waters only by or with the use of hook and line gear and spearing.
entries.full: Vessel limits: 60 (Gulf), 30 (Atlantic). Atlantic 20 in fork length minimum is in r. 68B-41.003 (not read; from FWC).
entries.scope: Florida Waters; gear rule within or without.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: .004 1 May 2022 and .006 1 Sep 2013 match flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Blue runner: 100 per person
entries.effect: Blue runner limit is 100 per person per day, within or without Florida Waters.
entries.excerpt: A recreational harvester may not harvest within or without Florida Waters or land more than 100 blue runner per day or possess within or without Florida Waters more than 100 blue runner.
entries.scope: State and federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 3 Jan 2014 matches flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Blackfin tuna: 2 per person or 10 per vessel
entries.effect: Blackfin tuna 2 per person per day, or 10 per vessel if that is greater; within or without Florida Waters.
entries.excerpt: (1) ... a recreational harvester harvesting blackfin tuna may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land more than 2 blackfin tuna per day. (2) ... may not collectively harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land more than 10 blackfin tuna per day or 2 per harvester per day, whichever is greater.
entries.scope: State and federal waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Jan 2020 matches flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Spanish mackerel: 15 per person; spear not excluded as gear in state waters
entries.effect: Spanish mackerel 15 per person per day; spearing is a listed gear in Florida Waters. Federal Atlantic gear rules differ (see cfr-622-375).
entries.excerpt: [.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest from Florida Waters more than 15 Spanish mackerel per day. [.006(1)] A person may harvest or attempt to harvest Spanish mackerel from Florida Waters only by or with the use of a beach or haul seine, a cast net, hook and line gear, or by spearing.
entries.full: 12 in fork length minimum is in r. 68B-23.003 (not read; from FWC and 50 C.F.R. 622.380).
entries.scope: Florida Waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: .004 25 Aug 2021 and .006 5 Sep 2019 match flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Atlantic king mackerel: 2 per person; hook and line or spearing
entries.effect: In the Atlantic king mackerel fishery the recreational limit is 2 per person per day and only hook and line or spearing may be used.
entries.excerpt: [(2)(a)] Any person harvesting king mackerel from the Atlantic fishery who does not meet the requirements and conditions established in subsection (1) and paragraph (2)(b), shall be subject to a bag limit of two fish per person, per day. [(4)] No person shall harvest king mackerel in the Atlantic fishery other than with hook and line gear, or by spearing.
entries.full: 'Atlantic fishery' is defined in r. 68B-30.002 (not read). FWC applies the Atlantic limit to Atlantic state waters excluding Monroe County.
entries.scope: Atlantic king mackerel fishery.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 25 Aug 2021 matches flrules. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Gulf-Atlantic king mackerel: 3 per person
entries.effect: King mackerel limit of 3 per person per day in the Gulf-Atlantic fishery (FWC: Gulf state waters and all of Monroe County).
entries.excerpt: three fish per person, per day
entries.full: Summarised: (1) sets three fish per person per day unless reduced to one under stated conditions; (5) lets FWC adjust the limit annually from 1 July after a hearing. Chapter 68B-12 has no gear rule (r. 68B-12.006 read).
entries.scope: Gulf-Atlantic king mackerel fishery.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 25 Aug 2021 matches flrules. Fishery boundary in r. 68B-12.002 not read. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: Biscayne National Park: larger minimum sizes and a 10-fish aggregate
entries.effect: Inside Biscayne National Park several reef fish have larger minimum sizes, and a 10-fish Major Finfish Aggregate applies.
entries.excerpt: [.003] Gray Triggerfish - 14 inches fork length; Bluestriped grunt - 10 inches total length; White grunt - 8 inches total length; Red Grouper - 24 inches total length; Gray Snapper - 12 inches total length; Lane Snapper - 10 inches total length; Mutton Snapper - 19 inches total length; Schoolmaster - 12 inches total length; Yellowtail Snapper - 14 inches total length. [.004(1)] A recreational harvester may not harvest or possess more than 10 fish from the Major Finfish Aggregate in any combination in or on the waters of Biscayne National Park, or land more than 10 fish from the Major Finfish Aggregate within Biscayne National Park, regardless of where harvested.
entries.full: Transit exception for fish taken outside the park with gear stowed. 'Major Finfish Aggregate' is defined in r. 68B-7.002 (amended 17 Sep 2025, not read).
entries.scope: Biscayne National Park waters.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: .003 and .004 1 Jul 2020 match flrules. See a1's fac-68b-7-008-5 for the seasonal bonefish closure. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: matched apart from paragraph labels or typography.

entries.title: Species with no bag limit: above 2 fish or 100 lb is a commercial quantity
entries.effect: For a species with no bag limit, taking more than the greater of 2 fish or 100 lb per person per day counts as commercial quantities needing a saltwater products licence. FWC presents this as the default recreational bag limit; strictly it is a licensing threshold.
entries.excerpt: With respect to those species for which no bag limit has been established, more than 100 pounds per person per day, provided that the harvesting of two fish or less per person per day shall not be considered commercial quantities regardless of aggregate weight
entries.scope: State waters and landings.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: 2026 statute text on Online Sunshine. Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: 2026 Atlantic red snapper: closed outside 9 to 22 Oct
entries.effect: Atlantic red snapper closed within or without Florida waters of the Atlantic except 9 to 22 Oct 2026; 1 per person, no minimum size, trip declaration required, until the order expires 31 Dec 2026.
entries.excerpt: No recreational harvester shall harvest within or without Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean or possess within or without Florida Waters of the Atlantic Ocean any red snapper outside of the open seasons identified in paragraph 3. ... There is no minimum size limit for red snapper applicable to recreational harvesters ... Only use hook and line, bandit gear, handline, and spear.
entries.full: Signed 22 Sep 2026; effective on execution; expires 11:59 p.m. 31 Dec 2026. Harvest dates 'October 9, 2026, through October 22, 2026'. Bag: 'no more than 1 red snapper per day'. Trip declaration through the FWC Atlantic Red Snapper Reporting System before each trip. FWC may seek a December 2026 season after consulting NMFS. Runs alongside Florida's federal exempted fishing permit.
entries.scope: Atlantic, state and federal waters (for Florida EFP participants in federal waters).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: FWC executive orders are published only on myfwc.com and are not on the project's primary-source list; the PDF is the instrument itself. No 2026 summer Atlantic season is recited; news reports say state waters closed 22 Sep 2026.

entries.effect: Gulf state-water greater amberjack closed from 12:01 a.m. 14 Oct 2026 to 31 Aug 2027. The order expires 12:01 a.m. 1 Nov 2026; r. 68B-14.004(1) keeps the closure to 31 Aug 2027.
entries.excerpt: the 2026-27 recreational season for greater amberjack in state waters of the Gulf of America shall close effective 12:01 a.m. local time, October 14, 2026

entries.scope: Gulf state waters.

Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: the order expires 12:01 a.m. 1 Nov 2026 (OCR text of the scan, secondary); r. 68B-14.004(1) then keeps Gulf state waters closed 1 Nov to 31 Dec and 1 Jan to 31 Aug 2027. entries.title: 2026 Atlantic gag: state waters closed from Aug 2, 2026
entries.effect: Gag closed in Atlantic state waters, including all state waters of Monroe County, from 12:01 a.m. 2 Aug 2026 through 31 Dec 2026; the order expires 12:01 a.m. 1 Jan 2027, after which r. 68B-14.0039(2) keeps it closed to 30 Apr 2027. Black grouper not named.
entries.excerpt: In state waters of the Atlantic Ocean, including all state waters of Monroe County, the closed season for the recreational harvest and possession of gag grouper shall be from August 2, 2026, through December 31, 2026.
entries.full: From FWC release of 13 May 2026 and govdelivery bulletin: 'state waters of the Atlantic Ocean, including all state waters off Monroe County'; closes '12:01 a.m. on August 2'. Mirrors 91 FR 21389.

entries.title: 2026 Gulf gag: state waters closed from 1 Oct 2026 (not Monroe)
entries.effect: Gag closed in Gulf state waters, except all waters of Monroe County, from 12:01 a.m. 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Dec 2026; the order expires 12:01 a.m. 1 Jan 2027, after which r. 68B-14.0039(1) keeps it closed until 1 Sep 2027.
entries.excerpt: A recreational harvester may not harvest any gag grouper in or from state waters of the Gulf of America, except in all waters of Monroe County, or possess any gag grouper while in or on state waters of the Gulf of America, except in all waters of Monroe County, from October 1 through December 31, 2026.
entries.full: From FWC release 7 Aug 2026 ('Sept. 1 through Sept. 30', closing 12:01 a.m. Oct. 1; 'excluding all state waters off Monroe County').

entries.title: 2026 Atlantic snowy grouper: closed from Jun 7, 2026
entries.effect: Snowy grouper closed in Atlantic state waters from 12:01 a.m. 7 Jun 2026 for the rest of 2026.

entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ: goliath, Nassau, speckled hind and warsaw prohibited; cubera and red snapper limits
entries.effect: In the South Atlantic EEZ goliath, Nassau, speckled hind and warsaw may not be harvested or possessed; cubera 30 in TL and larger limited to 2 per person and 2 per vessel off Florida; red snapper only in announced seasons.
entries.excerpt: (b)(1) Goliath grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ. ... (3) Speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ. ... (4) Nassau grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ. ... (c)(2) Red snapper may only be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ during the commercial and recreational seasons as specified in §§ 622.183(b)(5) and 622.193(y).
entries.full: (c)(1): 'No person may harvest more than two cubera snapper measuring 30 inches (76.2 cm), TL, or larger, per day in the South Atlantic EEZ off Florida and no more than two such cubera snapper in or from the South Atlantic EEZ off Florida may be possessed on board a vessel at any time.'
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ (and Gulf EEZ for Nassau).
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: last amended 83 FR 35434 (2018). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: matched apart from paragraph labels or typography.

entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ seasonal closures: shallow-water grouper, hogfish, red snapper, tilefish, snowy, red porgy, greater amberjack
entries.effect: Recurring South Atlantic EEZ closures: shallow-water grouper Jan to Apr; hogfish off Keys and east Florida Jan to Apr and Nov to Dec; blueline tilefish and snowy grouper outside May to Aug and May to Jun; red porgy outside May to Jun; greater amberjack in April.
entries.excerpt: (b)(1) ... January through April each year, no person may fish for, harvest, or possess in or from the South Atlantic EEZ any South Atlantic shallow-water grouper ... (b)(10) ... No person may fish for, harvest, or possess in or from the South Atlantic EEZ any greater amberjack ...
entries.full: (b)(4) hogfish recreational, Florida Keys and east coast of Florida: closed 'January through April and from November through December each year'. (b)(5) red snapper: seasons announced in the Federal Register. (b)(7) blueline tilefish: closed 'January 1 through April 30, and September 1 through December 31'. (b)(8) snowy: closed 'January 1 through April 30, and July 1 through December 31'. (b)(9) red porgy: same windows as snowy. (b)(10) greater amberjack: 'April 1 through April 30, each year'. SA shallow-water grouper (622.2): gag, black, red, scamp, red hind, rock hind, yellowmouth, yellowfin, graysby, coney.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ.

entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ minimum sizes
entries.effect: South Atlantic EEZ minimum sizes: gray snapper 12 in TL (larger than state 10 in); hogfish 16 in FL off Florida; greater amberjack 28 in FL; gray triggerfish 12 in FL.
entries.excerpt: All size limits in this section are minimum size limits unless specified otherwise ... A fish not in compliance with its size limit must be released immediately with a minimum of harm.
entries.full: Summarised table: vermilion 12 in TL; cubera, gray, yellowtail 12 in TL; mutton 18 in TL; lane 8 in TL; red, yellowfin, yellowmouth grouper and scamp 20 in TL; black grouper and gag 24 in TL; black sea bass 13 in TL (bag-limit fishers); gray triggerfish 12 in FL; hogfish 17 in FL off GA to NC and 16 in FL off Florida Keys, east Florida and Gulf south of 25 deg 09 min N; red porgy 14 in TL; greater amberjack 28 in FL (bag-limit fishers); almaco jack 20 in FL (no bag limit only).

entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: last amended 88 FR 65822 (2023). Browser check 30 Sep 2026: excerpt matched word for word at the source.

entries.title: South Atlantic EEZ bag limits
entries.effect: South Atlantic EEZ: 3 grouper and tilefish including no more than 1 gag or black grouper and no more than 1 scamp or yellowmouth grouper; private vessel limit 2 gag and 2 black grouper per day until 28 Oct 2026, then 2 gag and black grouper combined (fr-91-61160); 10 snappers including 5 mutton; 5 vermilion; 1 red snapper in season; 1 hogfish off Florida; 7 black sea bass; 1 red porgy; 1 greater amberjack; 20 other snapper-grouper, no more than 10 of any one species.
entries.excerpt: [(b)(2)(v):] (v) No more than one fish may be a scamp or a yellowmouth grouper, combined. [(b)(8):] Within the 20-fish bag limit, no more than 10 fish can be of any one of these single snapper-grouper species. [(b)(2)(i)(A):] (A) In addition to the bag limits specified in this paragraph (b)(2)(i), for gag, the vessel limit for a vessel operating as a private recreational vessel may not exceed 2 fish per vessel per day. [(b)(2)(i)(C):] (C) ... for black grouper, the vessel limit for a vessel operating as a private recreational vessel may not exceed 2 fish per vessel per day.
entries.full: (b)(8) 20-fish aggregate excludes 'tomtate, South Atlantic snapper-grouper ecosystem component species (specified in table 2 of appendix A of this part), and those specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (7) and paragraphs (b)(9) and (10)'. Numbers summarised: (b)(1) greater amberjack 1; (b)(2) grouper and tilefish 3, snowy 1 per vessel, golden tilefish 1, blueline tilefish 2; (b)(4) snappers 10 with 5 mutton; (b)(5) vermilion 5; (b)(6) red porgy 1; (b)(7) black sea bass 7; (b)(9) red snapper 1; (b)(10) wreckfish 1 per vessel. Black grouper also 2 per private vessel per day.
entries.scope: South Atlantic EEZ.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026 and Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer (current) for the four quoted paragraphs. The scamp and yellowmouth sub-limit and the 10-of-one-species cap were missing before. The other numbers in the effect line are summarised, so the entry stays secondary. Re-read 11 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer (current; latest version 28 Oct 2026). Regulatory Amendment 36 is now rendered: "(A) The vessel limit for gag and black grouper on a vessel operating as a private recreational vessel is two fish per day in any combination. (B) The vessel limit for gag and black grouper on a vessel operating as a charter vessel or headboat is two fish per trip in any combination." entries.title: King and Spanish mackerel: federal gear list omits spears (Atlantic king and Spanish, Gulf king)
entries.effect: In the EEZ, the only gear for directed king mackerel fishing is rod and reel, handline, bandit gear and automatic reel (Atlantic) or hook-and-line (Gulf), and for Atlantic Spanish mackerel a list that also omits spears. Conservative reading: spearing these fish in federal waters is not authorized. Gulf Spanish mackerel and cobia allow all gear except certain nets.
entries.excerpt: (a) Authorized gear—(1) King and Spanish mackerel. Subject to the prohibitions on gear/methods specified in § 622.9, the following are the only fishing gears that may be used in the Gulf, Mid-Atlantic, and South Atlantic EEZ in directed fisheries for king and Spanish mackerel: (i) King mackerel, Atlantic migratory group— ... South of 34°37.3′ N. lat.—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, and rod and reel. (ii) King mackerel, Gulf migratory group—hook-and-line gear and, in the southern zone only, run-around gillnet. (iii) Spanish mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, rod and reel, cast net, run-around gillnet, and stab net. (iv) Spanish mackerel, Gulf migratory group—all gear except drift gillnet, long gillnet, and purse seine.
entries.full: (a)(2) cobia, Gulf migratory group (Gulf EEZ and South Atlantic EEZ south of the Florida/Georgia line): 'all gear except drift gillnet and long gillnet'. (b)(3): a person aboard a vessel with unauthorized gear (other than the listed gillnets) 'is subject to the bag limits for king and Spanish mackerel specified in § 622.382(a)(1)(ii) and (iv), respectively, and to the limit on cobia specified in § 622.383(b)'. Whether a recreational spearfisher is in a 'directed fishery' is not defined in 622.2.

entries.title: Marathon: no speargun use in any manmade canal
entries.effect: Inside the City of Marathon it is unlawful to use, fire or discharge a speargun on or below the surface of any manmade canal; the speargun is forfeited on conviction.
entries.excerpt: Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined above, on or below the surface of any manmade canal.
entries.full: Definition. A speargun is any device, whether commercially manufactured or handmade, which is so designed and constructed so as to be capable of forcefully discharging at great velocity any spear or any similar projectile in a direction determined by the user thereof for a distance greater than two (2) feet (24 inches), whether or not such spear or projectile is tethered to the firing apparatus or otherwise limited in its range. No distinction shall be made as to the mechanical construction or physical means utilized in such devices to create the potential energy necessary to eject or fire such spear or similar projectiles. Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined above, on or below the surface of any manmade canal. Penalties. Any person convicted of a violation of this section shall be penalized in accordance with Section 1-7. In addition, any person convicted of a violation of this section shall forfeit the speargun used by such person in committing such offense to the City for destruction in the same manner as forfeited firearms are disposed of by the Sheriff. (Code 1999, § 13-5)
entries.scope: All manmade canals within the City of Marathon city limits (Monroe County). The section names no canal list or map.

entries.title: Town of Palm Beach: no spearfishing gear on five named public beaches

entries.excerpt: The possession of spearfishing equipment is prohibited and declared to be unlawful on those areas of the public beach within the town specifically designated by the town for public use described as follows:
entries.full: (b) Prohibited. The possession of spearfishing equipment is prohibited and declared to be unlawful on those areas of the public beach within the town specifically designated by the town for public use described as follows: (1) Phipps Ocean Park, consisting of approximately 1,200 linear feet adjacent to the waters of the Atlantic Ocean. (2) Midtown Beach, beginning at an area 150 feet north of Royal Palm Way, south to Gulfstream Road. (3) The Clarke Avenue Beach area from Barton Avenue on the north to Sea Breeze Avenue on the south. (4) The public beach known as Kreusler Park running north of the City of Lake Worth casino property extending approximately 500 feet northerly therefrom. (5) The Inlet Dock facility located at the Palm Beach Inlet (Lake Worth Inlet). (c) Regulated. On those areas of the public beach not described above, spearfishing equipment shall be carried in a manner so as to keep the equipment from being accidentally or intentionally discharged and shall be carried in a manner so as not to be cocked, loaded, engaged or aimed. Definitions in (a): 'Beaches means that area abutting the Atlantic Ocean or Lake Worth consisting of predominately sand, whether below or above the mean high water mark. Spearfishing equipment means any spear, gig or lance intended for use of spearfishing and which is propelled by rubber bands, metal springs, or the explosion or expansion of powder, gas, or similar substance.' (Code 1982, § 14-33; Ord. No. 15-95, § 2, 9-12-95)

entries.title: Town of Palm Beach: diving off guarded beaches needs a buddy, cert card, BC and flag
entries.effect: Skin or scuba diving off lifeguarded Town beaches is unlawful unless divers use the buddy system, scuba divers carry a certification card, each diver has a BC, and each dive unit flies a dive flag.
entries.excerpt: It shall be unlawful to skin or scuba dive off public beaches operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town unless adequate safety precautions are taken.
entries.full: It shall be unlawful to skin or scuba dive off public beaches operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town unless adequate safety precautions are taken. (1) The "buddy" system must be used, making it necessary to have two or more people diving. It shall be unlawful to dive alone. (2) If scuba diving, each member must have a current nationally recognized open water certification card. (3) Each diver must have a buoyancy compensator capable of supporting the head of an unconscious diver above the water. (4) Each dive unit must have a diver's down flag. This flag must be free flying and clearly visible to boaters from a minimum of 100 feet in all directions. The flag must be a minimum of 12 inches by 12 inches and must have a red diagonal background with a white stripe. An international alpha flag may be used in lieu of the above flag. (Code 1982, § 14-64)

entries.excerpt: To cease fishing (including shark fishing and spear fishing) too close to bathers;
entries.full: (18) No person may deliberately disobey a reasonable command made while such person is using the beach or any structure thereon owned or operated by Escambia County. ... e. A reasonable command shall include, but not be limited to, the following commands: 1. To cease fishing (including shark fishing and spear fishing) too close to bathers;
entries.scope: Beaches and beach structures owned or operated by Escambia County.
entries.note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: NEW. Not a closure; popup note for Pensacola Beach and Perdido Key. The excerpt is an item in the list of reasonable commands under (18)e.

entries.cite: Gulf Islands National Seashore, 'Fishing in Florida' (nps.gov, last updated 28 Aug 2026)
entries.title: Gulf Islands NS: Florida water boundary and fishing closures
entries.effect: The Seashore's water runs north to the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and south one mile from the low tide line at Perdido Key, Fort Pickens and Santa Rosa, and 100 yards from the low tide line at Naval Live Oaks. Florida fishing regulations apply there; fishing is closed at the Fort Pickens ferry pier and at the designated swim beaches while lifeguards are on duty.
entries.excerpt: All fishing regulations for national seashore waters in Florida correspond with Florida fishing regulations. In the Perdido Key, Fort Pickens, and Santa Rosa Areas the national seashore boundary extends on the north to the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and on the south one mile from the low tide line of the island. At Naval Live Oaks the national seashore boundary extends 100 yards from the low tide line.
entries.scope: Gulf Islands National Seashore, Florida District waters.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 from the page DOM. Same page: 'Fishing is prohibited in the following locations when lifeguards are on duty: the designated swim beaches located at Johnson Beach, Langdon Beach, Opal Beach, and Ship Island (formerly known as West ship & East Ship Islands).' and 'The Fort Pickens ferry pier is closed to fishing and netting.' A park web page, not a regulation; the boundary itself is set by the Seashore's enabling legislation, not read here.

entries.title: National parks: a speargun is a weapon, and a loaded speargun in any vessel is prohibited
entries.effect: In National Park System units (Biscayne, Dry Tortugas, Everglades, Canaveral NS, Gulf Islands NS, Timucuan), a speargun is a weapon. Possessing, carrying or using one is prohibited unless the taking of fish is authorized under § 2.3. Carrying or possessing a loaded weapon in a vessel is prohibited, anchored or under way; the only exception, a vessel not propelled by machinery and used as a shooting platform, does not fit a dive boat. Unload before you climb back aboard. Read with § 2.3(e), salt-water spearfishing otherwise follows state law unless the park designates otherwise.
entries.excerpt: [§ 1.4(a):] Weapon means a firearm, compressed gas or spring-powered pistol or rifle, bow and arrow, crossbow, blowgun, speargun, hand-thrown spear, slingshot, irritant gas device, explosive device, or any other implement designed to discharge missiles [§ 2.4(b)(1):] (i) Possessing a weapon, trap or net (ii) Carrying a weapon, trap or net (iii) Using a weapon, trap or net [§ 2.4(b)(2)(i)(B):] (B) The taking of fish is authorized by law in accordance with § 2.3 of this part. [§ 2.4(c):] (c) Carrying or possessing a loaded weapon in a motor vehicle, vessel or other mode of transportation is prohibited, except that carrying or possessing a loaded weapon in a vessel is allowed when such vessel is not being propelled by machinery and is used as a shooting platform in accordance with Federal and State law.
entries.full: [§ 2.4(b)(3)(i):] (i) Traps, nets and unloaded weapons may be possessed within a temporary lodging or mechanical mode of conveyance when such implements are rendered temporarily inoperable or are packed, cased or stored in a manner that will prevent their ready use.
entries.scope: All National Park System units in Florida.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer. Park-specific rules add to this: § 7.27 (Dry Tortugas: spearfishing prohibited park-wide), § 7.45 (Everglades: hook and line only).

entries.cite: Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary Management Review: Blueprint for Restoration, final rule, 90 FR 6104 (Jan. 17, 2025)
entries.title: FKNMS Restoration Blueprint final rule: French Reef SPA, Rock Key SPA and Looe Key SUA eliminated
entries.effect: The Blueprint final rule eliminates the French Reef and Rock Key Sanctuary Preservation Areas and the Looe Key Special-Use (Research Only) Area as zones. The rule does not take effect in state sanctuary waters, where Florida's Governor objected, so Rock Key SPA, which lies in state waters, stays under the 1997 zoning. NOAA has not published the effective-date announcement the rule promised, and eCFR still prints all three zones.
entries.excerpt: NOAA's final rule eliminates five existing marine zones including one Conservation Area (Looe Key SUA), two SPAs (Rock Key and French Reef) and two WMAs (Little Crane Key and Tidal Flat South of Marvin Key). These existing marine zones are eliminated due to resource condition changes and an opportunity to evaluate different management regimes. The elimination of these zones removes restrictions on fishing in these areas.
entries.scope: FKNMS federal waters (and state waters only if the Governor did not certify objection).
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 from federalregister.gov raw text (doc 2025-00496), response to comments at 90 FR 6128. DATES field: '... if the Governor of the State of Florida certifies to the Secretary of Commerce during that same review period that any such regulation is unacceptable, the regulation(s) will not take effect in State waters of the sanctuary. ... NOAA will publish an announcement of the effective date of the final regulations in the Federal Register.' No such announcement found (searches 7 Oct 2026: CFR 15 pt 922 since 1 Jun 2024; 'Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary' 2026; 'Restoration Blueprint'/'Blueprint for Restoration' after 17 Jan 2025). Rock Key SPA remains in NOAA's 28 Apr 2026 zone layer flagged state waters, consistent with the split. Re-checked 11 Nov 2026: Federal Register API searches for 15 C.F.R. part 922 and the term 'Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary' from 6 Oct 2026 return no codification or effective-date notice. The state and federal split stands.

entries.cite: Executive Order 14430, Restoring American Saltwater Angling and Recreation, 91 FR 60293 (Sept. 22, 2026)
entries.title: EO 14430: agencies to initiate suspension, revision or rescission of regulations burdening anglers
entries.effect: No legal effect on any closure by itself. Directs Interior, Agriculture, Commerce and the Army Corps to begin, by 17 Oct 2026, action to suspend, revise or rescind regulations that overly burden boaters, anglers and outdoor businesses. Watch for proposals touching FKNMS, NPS compendia, refuges and fishery closures.
entries.excerpt: Sec. 5. Rescission of Regulations that Restrict Marine Infrastructure and Access. (a) Within 30 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works shall, consistent with applicable law, take steps to initiate action to suspend, revise, or rescind regulations that overly burden boaters, anglers, and outdoor businesses.
entries.scope: Federal agencies; no Florida-specific text.
entries.note: Signed 17 Sep 2026, published 22 Sep 2026, doc 2026-19417. Read 7 Oct 2026 from federalregister.gov raw text. No agency document citing '14430' found through 7 Oct 2026. The URL slug was built from the title; the document number 2026-19417 is confirmed. Re-checked 11 Nov 2026: a Federal Register full-text search for '14430' returns only the order itself (2026-19417); no NOAA, NPS, FWS or FKNMS document cites it, and no document in 50 C.F.R. parts 17, 26, 27, 32, 600, 622, 640, 36 C.F.R. part 7, 15 C.F.R. part 922 or 33 C.F.R. part 334 was published between 6 Oct and 12 Nov 2026 that changes a Florida spearfishing rule.

entries.effect: From 28 Oct 2026 a private recreational vessel in the South Atlantic EEZ may keep no more than two gag and black grouper per day in any combination, and a charter vessel or headboat two per trip. Until then the limits are 2 gag and 2 black grouper separately.

entries.cite: Palm Beach County Code, App. G, ch. 13, art. II, div. 1, §§ 13-31 to 13-39 (Laws of Fla. ch. 59-1702)
entries.title: Palm Beach County: no underwater spearfishing at night or within any inlet
entries.effect: In all Palm Beach County salt waters, underwater spearfishing is banned from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise, banned at all times within any inlet, banned within 150 ft of an anchored boat with people fishing, and needs a diver-down flag in the Intracoastal waters, within 200 yd of inlet jetties, and more than 150 yd offshore.
entries.excerpt: Sec. 13-32. No person shall engage in underwater spear fishing in any of the salt waters of Palm Beach County, Florida, during the period of time from one (1) hour after sunset to one (1) hour before sunrise. Sec. 13-33. No person shall at any time engage in underwater spear fishing within any inlet in Palm Beach County, Florida.
entries.full: § 13-35: 'No person shall engage in underwater spear fishing in the salt waters of Palm Beach County, Florida, within one hundred fifty (150) feet of any anchored boat containing a person or persons engaged in fishing provided that this section shall not apply to those persons who were engaged in underwater spear fishing in the salt waters described in this section immediately prior to and at the time that such boat was anchored.' Session law ch. 59-1702 (HB 1996, filed 18 Jun 1959) s. 1(b) defines underwater spear fishing as spearing 'while the person manipulating such instrument or implement is either under water or floating in the water or swimming', so it reaches freedivers as well as scuba. s. 1(d) 'Intercoastal Waters' are all county territorial waters except those in the Atlantic Ocean. s. 7: flag required within 200 yd of any inlet jetty, not applying inside 150 yd of MHW. s. 8: flag required more than 150 yd from MHW. s. 10 repeals ch. 31133 (1955). County code history notes cite 59-1702 ss. 2 to 9 for §§ 13-32 to 13-39.
entries.scope: All salt waters of Palm Beach County (night ban); every inlet in the county: Jupiter Inlet, Lake Worth Inlet, South Lake Worth (Boynton) Inlet, Boca Raton Inlet (inlet ban). 'Inlet' is undefined.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026: county code through api.municode.com (Supplement 126 Update 1, 7 Jul 2026) and the 1959 session law from the State Library scan (edocs.dlis.state.fl.us/fldocs/leg/actsflorida/1959/LOF1959V2Pt3Ch1670-1754.pdf, printed pp. 3261 to 3263). Wording matches apart from '(1)' numerals and capitalisation. FWC did not repeal 59-1702 in r. 68B-3.038. Applies to freedivers. regs.json already describes these rules but law.json had no entry; the inlet ban is drawn only at Lake Worth Inlet.

entries.title: Hollywood: no spearfishing within 100 yards of the public beach
entries.effect: Spearfishing is prohibited within 100 yards of Hollywood's public/municipal beach, which § 99.01 defines as running from mean high water to 50 yards offshore along the whole Hollywood oceanfront; loaded spearguns are barred on the beach and in public swimming areas.
entries.excerpt: (F) Spearfishing is prohibited within 100 yards of the public/municipal beach. It is unlawful to carry or possess a loaded spear gun on the public/municipal beach or in the public swimming areas. Participants must have fish bag and a raft.
entries.full: Lead-in: 'It shall be unlawful for any person to do any acts set forth below upon Hollywood Beach as described in § 99.01:' (E): 'Swim, bathe or participate in other water activities in the proximity of groins, jetties or other hazards, or, sit, stand, or perform any activity on these structures.' § 99.01 opens: 'All of the area lying east of the mean high water line and north of the common Hollywood-Hallandale city limits and south of an easterly extension of the south right-of-way of Magnolia Terrace and west of a point 50 yards east of said mean high water line;' and continues north to 'south of John U. Lloyd State Park and west of a point 50 yards east of said mean high water line, less that portion in the corporate city limits of Dania, Florida'. § 99.02(B)(4) allows snorkeling or scuba with a diver-down flag. History § 99.03: ('72 Code, § 7½-4) (Ord. O-74-24, passed 3-6-74; ... Am. Ord. O-2023-04, passed 4-4-23).
entries.scope: Atlantic Ocean off the Hollywood oceanfront, Hallandale Beach city line north to John U. Lloyd Beach State Park (less any part in Dania Beach). Conservative reading: 100 yd measured from the seaward edge of the defined beach, i.e. 150 yd from MHW.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in Chrome on American Legal (rendered page text). NEW: not in the 30 Sep sweep, which could not reach Hollywood. Ambiguity: the lead-in limits § 99.03 to acts 'upon Hollywood Beach' (MHW to 50 yd) while (F) reaches 100 yd 'of' the beach; the conservative reading gives (F) its full reach measured from the beach's seaward edge. Whole Hollywood code not yet searched for other spear rules.

entries.title: Pinellas County: manmade saltwater canals are hook and line, hand cast net or blue crab traps only
entries.effect: Taking saltwater fish in any manmade saltwater canal in Pinellas County by any other method, spearing included, is prohibited. The text reaches every manmade canal in the county, cities included.
entries.excerpt: (a) [Regulated.] It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take any saltwater fish, except by hook and line or handheld cast net or with no more than five blue-crab traps, within any manmade saltwater canal located in Pinellas County, Florida.
entries.full: (b) [Penalty.] The violation of this section is declared to be a criminal offense and misdemeanor within the meaning of F.S. § 775.08, and shall be punishable as provided by law. (Ord. No. 25-28, § 1, 12-16-25). Sits in ch. 14, art. III, div. 2 'Saltwater Fishing', whose footnote says 'The acts contained in this division retain their status as special acts. See charter § 5.02.' and cites former F.S. § 370.172(4) and § 125.01(4).
entries.scope: Every manmade saltwater canal in Pinellas County.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page. Adopted 16 Dec 2025. No canal dataset is drawn; treat every residential canal as closed to spearing.

entries.title: Naples: no diving, jumping or swimming within 100 ft of a public bridge
entries.effect: Diving or jumping from, or swimming within 100 feet of, any publicly accessible bridge in Naples is prohibited. The bridge buffers drawn on the map are wider.
entries.excerpt: No person shall dive or jump from or swim within 100 feet of any bridge accessible to the public located totally or partially within the corporate limits of the city. (Code 1957, § 7-4.1; Code 1994, § 78-3)
entries.scope: Public bridges in Naples.
entries.note: Read 8 Oct 2026 through Municode's content service in the author's Chrome.

entries.title: Town of Palm Beach: no fishing within 50 yards either side of guarded beaches; no swimming beyond 300 ft of them
entries.effect: Fishing, which includes spearfishing, is unlawful in the waters 50 yards north or south of any lifeguarded Town beach, and swimming beyond 300 ft (from mean low water) of a lifeguarded Town beach is unlawful.
entries.excerpt: (e) It shall be unlawful for any person to fish in the waters 50 yards in either direction north or south of any public beach operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town.
entries.full: § 74-162 history: (Ord. No. 8-96, § 1, 5-14-96; Ord. No. 21-10, § 1, 7-13-10; Ord. No. 003-2025, § 2, 3-4-25). § 74-197(a): 'It shall be declared unlawful for any person to swim beyond 300 feet of the shore of any public beach operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town. For the purposes of this section, the 300-foot distance shall be measured at right angles from the mean low water mark of the Atlantic Ocean.' (b) applies to flotation aids. (Code 1982, § 14-61). § 74-269(a)(1) names the public beaches as 'Phipps Ocean Park, Mid Town Beach, Clarke Avenue Beach and Kreusler Park' for its 400 ft watercraft exclusion.
entries.scope: Water off each lifeguarded Town of Palm Beach beach and 50 yd beyond each end (fishing); beyond 300 ft from MLW off those beaches (swimming).
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com (client 9332, product 11397). NEW. Ch. 74 art. III is Boats and Boating; the sweep's 'art. III' lead meant the art. II beach rules. Reading of (e) that closes more water: the whole water off the guarded beach plus a 50-yard band each side. Guarded beaches are not listed in § 74-162; § 74-269 names four. Second read 8 Oct 2026 through Municode's content service: § 74-162(b) also makes it unlawful to fish or cast a net from any town-owned bridge or dock (fishing only, not net casting, is allowed from Annie's Dock), 'This includes all town-owned areas adjacent to or under such town-owned bridge or dock.'

entries.title: Deerfield Beach: no swimming beyond 50 yards of the beach without lifeguard permission; no fishing off the beach 8 a.m. to dusk
entries.effect: Off the Deerfield Beach municipal beach, swimming more than 50 yards out from mean high water needs the supervising lifeguard's permission, and fishing off the beach (which includes shore-entry spearfishing) is unlawful from 8 a.m. to dusk.
entries.excerpt: (b) Swim outside an area extending 50 yards eastward from the mean highwater mark of the Atlantic Ocean at the municipal/public beaches, unless express permission has been obtained from the supervising lifeguard.
entries.full: Lead-in: 'It shall be unlawful for any person to do any acts set out in this section upon the municipal/public beaches of the city.' (p) 'Fish off of the municipal/public beaches, including the use of cast nets, from 8:00 a.m. to dusk.' § 50-2 extends the municipal/public beach to the wet sand seaward of mean high water.
entries.scope: Atlantic Ocean off the Deerfield Beach municipal beach: beyond 50 yd from MHW (swimming, without permission); shore-based fishing from the beach 8 a.m. to dusk.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com. NEW. Conservative readings: a freediver or snorkeler is swimming; spearfishing is fishing; the lead-in's 'upon the municipal/public beaches' does not stop (b) applying in the water because (b) itself describes water. Warn, not closed: lifeguard permission can lift (b), and (p) is a daytime shore rule.

entries.title: St. Petersburg: fishing prohibited in city park waters, at seven named bridge and right-of-way locations, and in the pier district unless posted or authorized
entries.effect: Fishing by any method is prohibited in city park waters except where signs allow it, at seven listed locations (the Snell Isle, Shore Acres and 40th Avenue bridges, the Treasure Island bascule bridge, Overlook Drive, Eden Isle Boulevard and other causeways, and city rights-of-way along Central Avenue and Grande Canal Boulevard), and anywhere in the municipal pier district unless the city has authorized it. 'Park waters' is not mapped.
entries.excerpt: [§ 21-44:] Fishing in Park waters is prohibited, regardless of the method used, except at such times and places which are designated with signs allowing such use by the POD. (Code 1992, § 21-44; Ord. No. 694-G, § 1, 11-4-2004) [§ 7-5(c):] (c) It shall be unlawful for any person to fish within any portion of the municipal pier district at any time of day unless the POD has explicitly authorized fishing to take place in that location and at that time.
entries.full: [§ 7-5(a):] (a) It shall be unlawful for any person to fish at the following locations at any time of day: (1) The public bridge, catwalk, sidewalk or public right-of-way that connects the western terminus of Central Avenue with Causeway Isles in the City. (2) The public bridge, catwalk, sidewalk or public right-of-way described as that portion of the Bascule Bridge that connects the City of Treasure Island, Florida, and the City of St. Petersburg, Florida. (3) The Snell Isle Bridge, Shore Acres Bridge, 40th Avenue Bridge, or the approaches thereto. (4) Overlook Drive Bridge entrance to Venetian Isles and the approaches thereto. (5) City right-of-way areas along Grande Canal Boulevard. (6) The causeway connecting Shore Acres and Mermaid Point N.E. also known as Bayou Grande Boulevard and Mermaid Point Northeast. (7) The public causeway or bridge described as that portion of Eden Isle Boulevard N.E. that connects Snell Isle with Eden Isles.
entries.scope: City of St. Petersburg.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page (§ 21-44) and on 8 Oct 2026 through Municode's content service (§ 7-5, node PTIISTPECO_CH7BOBEWA_ARTIINGE_S7-5FIRESPAR). Because § 7-5 bars fishing at the listed bridges, the 100 yd bridge buffer arguably does not attach to them; the map keeps their buffers drawn (the reading that closes more water).
