entries.title: National wildlife refuges: using or possessing spears, gigs or other weapons is prohibited unless a refuge rule authorizes it
entries.effect: On a national wildlife refuge, using or possessing spears, gigs or other weapons is prohibited except as subchapter C authorizes. Treat refuge waters as closed to spearing unless part 32 names spearing for that refuge, and keep a speargun broken down and stowed when crossing them.
entries.excerpt: The use or possession of cross bows, bows and arrows, air guns, spears, gigs, or other weapons on national wildlife refuges is prohibited except as may be authorized under the provision of this subchapter C.
entries.scope: Every national wildlife refuge, refuge waters included.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer. Whether 'possession' reaches a stowed speargun aboard a vessel transiting refuge waters is not settled by the text; the map treats refuge waters as closed to spearing. See cfr-50-27-21 for the Key West and Great White Heron conflict.

entries.title: Everglades NP: gear and catch that are illegal in the park may cross it only on the named passes
entries.effect: Gear legal in state waters, and fish legal in state waters but illegal to possess in Everglades National Park, may be carried through the park only over Indian Key, Sand Fly, Rabbit Key and Chokoloskee passes and across Chokoloskee Bay, on the most direct route to or from Everglades City, Chokoloskee Island or Fakahatchee Bay. A speargun and speared fish fall in that class.
entries.excerpt: (9) Nets and gear that are legal to use in State waters, and fish and other edible or non-edible sea life that are legally acquired in State waters but are illegal to possess in the waters of Everglades National Park may be transported through the park only over Indian Key Pass, Sand Fly Pass, Rabbit Key Pass, Chokoloskee Pass and across Chokoloskee Bay, along the most direct route to or from Everglades City, Chokoloskee Island or Fakahatchee Bay.
entries.scope: Everglades National Park waters, Ten Thousand Islands side.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer.

entries.title: National parks: fresh waters are hook and line only
entries.effect: In park fresh waters, fishing by any method other than an attended hook and line is prohibited, so spearing is prohibited there.
entries.excerpt: (d) The following are prohibited: (1) Fishing in fresh waters in any manner other than by hook and line, with the rod or line being closely attended.
entries.scope: Fresh waters inside National Park System units.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer.

entries.title: Kings Bay: all waterborne activity, spear fishing included, prohibited next to the sanctuaries and the four springs while the seasonal provisions run
entries.effect: Within the specified distances of the Kings Bay manatee sanctuaries and of Three Sisters, House, Jurassic and Idiot's Delight No. 2 springs, all waterborne activity, fishing by spear included, is prohibited while paragraph (c)(14)(v) or (vi) is in effect; the two together run 15 Nov to 31 Mar and 1 Apr to 14 Nov. Paragraph (ix)(C) lists diving from the surface onto a resting or feeding manatee.
entries.excerpt: (iv) Time and area prohibitions. When the provisions of paragraphs (c)(14)(v) or (vi) of this section are in effect (November 15 through March 31 and April 1 through November 14, respectively), all waterborne activities, including swimming, diving (including skin and scuba diving), snorkeling, water skiing, surfing, fishing (including with hook and line, by cast net, or spear), and the use of water vehicles ... are prohibited in areas that are adjacent to and within specified distances from the existing manatee sanctuaries located in Kings Bay (defined in paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(7) of this section) and the springs defined in paragraph (c)(14)(ii) of this section: Three Sisters Springs, House Spring, Jurassic Spring, and Idiot's Delight Number 2 Spring. ... (C) Diving from the surface on to a resting or feeding manatee(s).
entries.scope: Kings Bay, Crystal River (Citrus County).
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer. The 'specified distances' are set in (c)(14)(v) and (vi), not read in this pass; the refuge and sanctuary polygons already on the map are drawn closed.

entries.cite: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Crystal River NWR fishing page; 50 C.F.R. § 27.21
entries.title: Crystal River NWR: no fishing in refuge waters
entries.effect: The Service states that no fishing is allowed in Crystal River NWR waters (the interior of Three Sisters Springs, the King Spring and Tarpon Hole area, and the waters around Warden Key) and that the manatee sanctuaries prohibit all fishing. Part 32 does not open the refuge, so § 27.21 closes it.
entries.excerpt: There is no fishing allowed in refuge waters (less than 5 percent of all waters in King Bay), including the interior springs of Three Sisters Springs, the King Spring/Tarpon Hole area, and Warden Key’s surrounding waters. In addition, all established manatee sanctuaries (closed waters) prohibit all fishing.
entries.scope: Crystal River NWR, Kings Bay.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on fws.gov. An agency web page, not regulation text; the authority is § 27.21 (entry cfr-50-27-21), which this page agrees with. The refuge zone on the map is drawn closed from 8 Oct 2026 (it was a warning).

entries.title: Federal waters: fish must be landed with head and fins intact
entries.effect: Finfish from the Gulf EEZ, and South Atlantic snapper-grouper from the South Atlantic EEZ, must be kept with head and fins intact. Snapper-grouper may be gutted, gilled and scaled but are otherwise kept whole. Filleting on the boat before landing is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: [§ 622.10(a):] (a) Finfish in or from the Gulf EEZ or Caribbean EEZ, except as specified in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, must be maintained with head and fins intact. [§ 622.186(a):] (a) South Atlantic snapper-grouper in or from the South Atlantic EEZ must be maintained with head and fins intact, except as specified in paragraph (b) of this section. Such fish may be eviscerated, gilled, and scaled, but must otherwise be maintained in a whole condition.
entries.scope: Gulf and South Atlantic EEZ.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the eCFR renderer. The state rule is r. 68B-14.006(4) (entry fac-68b-14-006-4).

entries.title: Saltwater fishing regulation is reserved to the state, with an exception for fishing from local government property
entries.effect: The power to regulate taking or possessing saltwater fish is reserved to the state. A local government may still prohibit saltwater fishing from real property it owns, for public health, safety or welfare. City and county ordinances that reach open water stand on contested ground; rules about city piers, parks and beaches fit the exception. The map treats every local ordinance as live.
entries.excerpt: The power to regulate the taking or possession of saltwater fish, as defined in s. 379.101, is expressly reserved to the state. This section does not prohibit a local government from prohibiting, for reasons of protecting the public health, safety, or welfare, saltwater fishing from real property owned by that local government.
entries.scope: Statewide; local ordinances.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on flsenate.gov. This, not § 790.33, is the statute a local spearfishing ordinance has to survive. Special acts printed in county codes (Laws of Florida) are state law and are not displaced by it in the same way. No court decision applying it to a spearfishing ordinance was found in this pass; the search was not exhaustive.

entries.title: No jumping or diving from a publicly owned bridge
entries.effect: A pedestrian may not jump or dive from a publicly owned bridge, posted or not. Entering the water from a bridge deck to dive under it is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: (17) No pedestrian may jump or dive from a publicly owned bridge. Nothing in this provision requires the state or any political subdivision of the state to post signs notifying the public of this provision.
entries.scope: Every publicly owned bridge in Florida.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on flsenate.gov. Several cities add their own bridge rules (Naples § 42-3: no swimming within 100 ft of any public bridge).

entries.title: Licence in personal possession; a dive boat's vessel licence covers its paying divers; spiny lobster permit
entries.effect: Carry the licence in personal possession while taking or possessing saltwater fish. Divers aboard a vessel that carries scuba divers for a fee and holds the right vessel licence do not need individual licences or permits. Taking or possessing spiny lobster recreationally requires the annual spiny lobster permit.
entries.excerpt: [(3):] ... must be in the personal possession of the person to whom it is issued while the person is taking, attempting to take, or possessing game, freshwater or saltwater fish, or fur-bearing animals. [(7)(f):] (f) If the operator of a vessel that carries scuba divers for a fee, either directly or indirectly, maintains the appropriate vessel license under this subsection based upon the number of persons the vessel is licensed to carry and the applicable permits, the individual scuba divers engaging in taking or attempting to take saltwater products are not required to obtain individual fishing licenses or any applicable permits. [(8)(d):] (d) An annual spiny lobster permit for a resident or nonresident to take or possess any spiny lobster for recreational purposes from any waters of the [...]
entries.scope: Statewide.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on flsenate.gov. The (8)(d) passage was returned up to the word shown; the rest of the sentence was not read. The free shoreline licence does not cover a diver (entry fs-379-354).

entries.title: Divers-down flag size, the slow-down distances for other boats, and when the flag must come down
entries.effect: The flag is at least 12 by 12 inches displayed from the water and 20 by 24 inches displayed from a vessel. Other vessels within 100 ft of the device in a river, inlet or navigation channel, or 300 ft elsewhere, must slow to the speed needed to keep headway and steerage. The device may not be displayed once all divers are aboard or ashore, and a vessel may not run with it displayed unless divers are in the water.
entries.excerpt: [(1)(c)1.:] 1. Contains a divers-down symbol that is at least 12 inches by 12 inches in dimension when displayed from the water or at least 20 by 24 inches in dimension when displayed from a vessel [(6):] (6) A vessel other than a law-enforcement or rescue vessel that approaches within 100 feet of a divers-down warning device on a river, inlet, or navigation channel, or within 300 feet of a divers-down warning device on waters other than a river, inlet, or navigation channel, must proceed no faster than is necessary to maintain headway and steerageway. [(7):] (7) A divers-down warning device may not be displayed once all divers are aboard or ashore. A person may not operate any vessel displaying a divers-down warning device unless the vessel has one or more divers in the water.
entries.scope: Statewide.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on flsenate.gov.

entries.title: Steinhatchee River: fresh water by statute from its source to its mouth
entries.effect: The statute makes the whole Steinhatchee River fresh water, mouth included, so spearing on it is prohibited and a speargun may not be used or possessed on it (r. 68A-23.002(7)). It is the only river the fisheries statute names.
entries.excerpt: The Steinhatchee River shall be considered fresh water from its source to mouth.
entries.scope: Steinhatchee River (Dixie and Taylor counties).
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on flsenate.gov. The river is drawn as a line along its OpenStreetMap centreline; the exact point the statute calls the mouth is not defined, so the line runs to the end of the mapped river in Deadman Bay.

entries.title: State parks: devices that fire a projectile may not be used or openly displayed
entries.effect: In any state park, using or openly displaying a device that fires a dart or projectile is prohibited, except gigs where gigs may be legally used for saltwater fishing. Keep spearguns cased and out of sight when carrying them through park land.
entries.excerpt: (10) Hunting and Firearms. ... No person shall use or openly display in any state park weapons such as firearms of any type, air rifles, spring guns, cross bows, bows and arrows, gigs (except in areas where gigs may be legally used for saltwater fishing), sling shots, electronic weapons, devices which fire a dart or projectile, or any other forms of weapons or trapping devices potentially dangerous to wildlife or human safety except when such weapons or traps are used for resource management purposes as authorized in this subsection.
entries.scope: All state parks.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 62D-2.014), current version effective 30 Apr 2007 per flrules.org. Spearfishing in park waters is closed separately by r. 62D-2.014(9) and r. 68B-20.003(2)(e).

entries.title: Fresh water: spear guns may not be used or possessed in or upon fresh waters
entries.effect: Using or possessing a speargun in or upon Florida's fresh waters is prohibited unless a rule or an executive director permit allows it. That includes carrying one aboard a boat on a freshwater river on the way to the coast.
entries.excerpt: (7) The use or possession of dynamite, traps, nets, seines, baskets, spear guns, any device capable of producing an electrical current sufficient to stun or shock freshwater fish, or any other fishing device or equipment except hook and line, rod and reel, bush hook, set line or trotline is expressly prohibited in or upon the fresh waters of the state unless specifically permitted by these rules or under permit issued by the executive director.
entries.scope: All fresh waters of the state.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68A-23.002), version effective 7 Jun 2022 per flrules.org. CORRECTS regs.json, which said the possession ban was weaker than FWC states and cited subsections (5) and (9) of an older numbering.

entries.title: Reef fish must be landed whole
entries.effect: Reef fish taken in state or adjacent federal waters must be landed whole. Possessing them deheaded, filleted, skinned or scaled on the water, on a pier, on a fishing bridge or on a jetty is prohibited. Gutting and gill removal are not.
entries.excerpt: (4) Landed in Whole Condition Requirement - Except as provided elsewhere in this rule, all fish harvested from Florida or adjacent federal Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) waters pursuant to the requirements of this chapter shall be landed in a whole condition. The possession, while in or on state waters, on any public or private fishing pier, on a bridge or catwalk attached to a bridge from which fishing is allowed, or on any jetty, of such fish that have been deheaded, sliced, divided, filleted, ground, skinned, scaled or deboned is prohibited. Mere evisceration or "gutting" of fish, or mere removal of gills from fish, before landing is not prohibited.
entries.scope: Reef fish (ch. 68B-14), state waters and adjacent EEZ.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68B-14.006), effective 1 Apr 2020 per flrules.org.

entries.title: Reef fish: a venting tool or descending device must be ready aboard
entries.effect: Anyone on a vessel harvesting the listed reef fish in or from Florida waters, spearfishing from the boat included, must be able to reach a venting tool or a rigged descending device.
entries.excerpt: (3) Descending device or venting tool. While harvesting or attempting to harvest, including catch and release, in or from Florida waters the species listed in subsection 68B-14.001(2), F.A.C., as well as goliath grouper and Nassau grouper, persons on board a vessel must be able to access a venting tool or a descending device that is rigged and ready to use.
entries.scope: State waters, from a vessel.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68B-14.005), effective 1 Apr 2023 per flrules.org. The federal South Atlantic rule (cfr-622-188-a4) likewise has no spearfishing exemption.

entries.title: Snook: hook and line only, no spearing, and no snook aboard together with spear gear
entries.effect: Snook may be taken only by hook and line, inside or outside Florida waters. Spearing is prohibited, and possessing a snook while also possessing gear not allowed by subsection (1), such as a speargun, is prohibited. A hook-caught snook and a speargun on the same boat is a violation.
entries.excerpt: (1) Allowed Gear and Method of Harvest - Within or without Florida Waters, a person may harvest or attempt to harvest a snook only by or with the use of hook and line gear. ... (c) A person may not harvest or attempt to harvest a snook by spearing the snook ... (3) A person may not possess a snook while also in possession of, using, or transporting a net, seine, or other fishing gear that is not expressly permitted in subsection (1). This prohibition does not apply to a person aboard a vessel who is in possession of a cast net if the cast net is stored off of the deck of the vessel.
entries.scope: State waters and beyond, for a Florida-landed snook.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68B-21.006), effective 1 Sep 2013 per flrules.org.

entries.title: Tarpon: spearing prohibited inside and outside Florida waters
entries.effect: Harvesting or attempting to harvest a tarpon by spearing, snagging or snatch hooking is prohibited, inside or outside Florida waters.
entries.excerpt: (2) Prohibited Gear and Methods of Harvest - A person may not harvest or attempt to harvest a tarpon within or without Florida Waters by spearing, snagging, or snatch hooking.
entries.scope: State waters and beyond.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68B-32.006).

entries.title: Permit and African pompano: the gear rule for adjacent federal waters
entries.effect: In state waters permit may be taken only by hook and line, and r. 68B-20.005 prohibits spearing both permit and African pompano. In adjacent federal waters this rule prohibits recreational harvest of either species by any gear other than hook and line or spearing, so it does not itself close the EEZ to spearing them. Paragraph (5)(a), an exception for permit, was not read in this pass.
entries.excerpt: [(2)(a):] In adjacent federal EEZ waters, the harvest or attempted harvest of any African pompano by or with the use of any gear other than hook and line gear or spearing is prohibited, while harvesting recreationally. [(3):] (3) Permit Gear - The harvest or attempted harvest of any permit in or from state waters by or with the use of any gear other than hook and line gear is prohibited. Except as provided in paragraph 68B-35.004(5)(a), F.A.C., the harvest or attempted harvest of any permit in adjacent federal EEZ waters by or with the use of any gear other than hook and line and spearing gear is prohibited.
entries.scope: State waters and adjacent EEZ.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on Cornell LII (R. 68B-35.004). OPEN: paragraph (5)(a) and the Special Permit Zone off south Florida were not read; until they are, the species cards keep the conservative federal-waters note. Read 11 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome (flrules.org .doc, tid 12228419): paragraph (5)(a) is only an exception for pompano or permit taken in adjacent federal waters as incidental bycatch in gill or entangling nets; it has nothing to do with spearing. The Special Permit Zone (r. 68B-35.002(14): south of 25°40′ N off Cape Florida, Biscayne Bay south of Rickenbacker Causeway, and further described waters) changes the size and bag limits in r. 68B-35.003 and 68B-35.0035, not the gear rule. So r. 68B-35.004(2)(a) and (3) leave spearing of African pompano and permit in adjacent federal waters unprohibited by chapter 68B-35, while r. 68B-20.005 lists both species with no geographic qualifier. The map keeps the reading that closes more water: do not spear either species anywhere. Question 29 is answered as far as the text goes; only FWC can say whether r. 68B-20.005 reaches federal waters.

entries.title: Boynton (South Lake Worth) Inlet: no swimming in the inlet, no entering the water from its jetties or bridge, and a closed area at the sand transfer plant
entries.effect: Swimming in the South Lake Worth Inlet is prohibited, as is diving, jumping or entering the inlet's water from any bulkhead, jetty, bridge or property abutting, over or near it. The ocean on the north side of the jetty within 75 ft of the sand transfer plant, or the plant's area of influence if that is larger, is a restricted area closed to swimming, snorkelling, diving and fishing.
entries.excerpt: [(a)(5):] (5) The water area of the Atlantic Ocean on the north side of the jetty of the inlet within seventy-five (75) feet of the sand transfer plant or the area of influence of the sand transfer plant, whichever is greater. [(b):] (b) It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to enter, climb on, deface, swim in, wade in, snorkel in, dive in, scuba dive in, surf in, boat in or otherwise be in or on any restricted area; ... to fish in, upon or from any portion of any restricted area [(d):] (d) It shall be unlawful for any person: (1) To swim in the South Lake Worth Inlet; (2) To dive, jump or gain access to the waters of the inlet from any bulkhead, jetty, bridge or property abutting, over or near the in[let]
entries.scope: Boynton Inlet.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page. The (d)(2) passage was returned up to the word shown.

entries.title: Clearwater: firing a spring, air or gas projectile weapon prohibited citywide, spearfishing excepted only where designated
entries.effect: Firing any weapon propelled by compressed air, gas expansion, a spring or other mechanical means is prohibited within Clearwater's city limits, which include water. Spearfishing is excepted only in an area designated as permissible by the city, the state or the United States; no such designation was found, so the whole city is drawn closed.
entries.excerpt: (1) It shall be unlawful for any person to fire any weapon from which a projectile is propelled by the action of compressed air, the expansion of gas or a spring, or other mechanical means, within the corporate limits of the city, except in lawful defense of life or property, or except by a law enforcement officer engaged in the discharge of his or her duties or in a duly licensed indoor or outdoor gun club, pistol range or rifle range. This section shall not be construed to prohibit spear fishing in any area where such activity has been designated as being permissible either by the city, the state or the United States.
entries.scope: City of Clearwater, including water within the city limits.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page. Same structure as Treasure Island § 22-2 (entry ti-22-2), which the map already draws citywide.

entries.cite: Laws of Fla. ch. 78-483, as amended by ch. 80-470 (Cape Coral Code § 12-11, editor's note)
entries.title: Cape Coral: manmade saltwater canals are hook and line or blue crab traps only
entries.effect: Taking saltwater fish in any manmade saltwater canal in Cape Coral by any method other than hook and line or up to five blue crab traps is prohibited, so spearing is prohibited in the canals.
entries.excerpt: Section 1. It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take any saltwater fish, except by hook and line or with no more than five blue crab traps within any man-made saltwater canal located in the City of Cape Coral.
entries.scope: Every manmade saltwater canal in Cape Coral.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page, where the city code quotes the act in an editor's note. Not drawn.

entries.cite: Laws of Fla. ch. 85-440, § 1 (Sanibel Code App. B, art. I, § 1)
entries.title: Sanibel: manmade saltwater canals are hook and line, hand cast net or blue crab traps only
entries.effect: Taking saltwater fish in any manmade saltwater canal in Sanibel by any method other than hook and line, a hand-held cast net or up to five blue crab traps is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take any saltwater fish, except by hook and line or hand-held cast net or with no more than five blue crab traps, within any manmade saltwater canal located in the City of Sanibel. (Laws of Fla., ch. 85-440, § 1)

entries.title: Naples: listed residential canals are hook and line, hand cast net or crab traps only
entries.effect: Taking saltwater fish in the residential manmade canals the act lists (Port Royal and others, each with an entrance point) by any method other than hook and line, hand-held cast nets or up to five crab traps is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take saltwater fish, except by hook and line, hand-held cast nets, and with no more than five (5) crab traps, in the residential, man-made saltwater canals in the City of Naples as defined herein.

entries.cite: Brevard County Code § 122-3(c) (Laws of Fla. ch. 93-376)
entries.title: Unincorporated Brevard: residential manmade saltwater canals are hook and line or hand cast net only
entries.effect: Taking fish from any residential manmade saltwater canal in unincorporated Brevard County by any method other than hook and line or a hand-thrown cast net is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: (c) Prohibited activity. It shall be a violation of this section to take fish from any residential, manmade, saltwater canal within the county by any means other than by hook and line or cast net thrown by hand.

entries.title: Satellite Beach: named residential canals are hook and line or hand cast net only
entries.effect: Taking fish from the fourteen manmade residential canals the section lists, the Grand Canal included, by any means other than hook and line or a hand-thrown cast net is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: It shall be unlawful for any person to catch or take fish from the following manmade saltwater residential canals by means other than hook-and-line or cast net thrown by hand: ... (12) The dredged mosquito control canal (Grand Canal) from the northern city limits to the southern city limits. ... (Code 1976, § 14-19)

entries.title: Unincorporated Collier: listed residential canals are hook and line, hand cast net or crab traps only
entries.effect: Taking saltwater fish in the residential manmade canals of unincorporated Collier County listed in Exhibit A (Isles of Capri first) by any method other than hook and line, hand-held cast nets or up to five crab traps is prohibited.
entries.excerpt: (a) It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take saltwater fish, except by hook and line, handheld cast nets, and with no more than five crab traps, in the residential, manmade saltwater canals in the unincorporated area of Collier County as defined herein.

entries.title: Volusia beaches: no swimming within 300 ft of a pier or jetty
entries.effect: On Volusia's beaches, swimming or bathing within 300 feet in any direction of a pier or jetty is prohibited, and so is swimming more than 300 feet from the water's edge unless it is a necessary incident to another permitted activity. A spearfisher in the water is swimming; the map draws 350 ft around the Ponce Inlet jetties.
entries.excerpt: (c) Swimming. No person except a lifeguard or other person actually engaged in a rescue attempt shall: (1) Swim or bathe more than 300 feet perpendicular from the water's edge except as a necessary incident to other activities permitted beyond such distance. (2) Swim or bathe within 300 feet measured in any direction from a pier or jetty.
entries.scope: Volusia County beaches (beach code, ch. 20).
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on the rendered Municode page. How far the beach code reaches inside cities and offshore is not settled here; the reading drawn treats the jetties as covered.

entries.title: Mexico Beach: no swimming in the canal boat channel or within 100 ft of either side of the jetties
entries.effect: Swimming is prohibited in the boat channel of the city canal from the uppermost marina to the Gulf low water mark, and within 100 feet on each side of the jetties at the entrance. A spearfisher is swimming, so the channel and its entrance are closed.
entries.excerpt: It shall be unlawful for any person to swim in the boat channel of the city canal in an area extending from the confines of the uppermost marina to the mean low water mark of the Gulf of Mexico, where the canal empties into the Gulf of Mexico. This prohibition includes the area 100 feet on each side of the jetties at the entrance to the Gulf.
entries.scope: Mexico Beach canal channel and entrance.
entries.note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in the author's Chrome on American Legal. The canal itself is not drawn; a marker sits at the entrance.

entries.title: Bradenton Beach parks: no fishing from a boat within 300 ft of a public beach, pier or fishing groin, nor in bathing areas
entries.effect: Within city parks, fishing offshore from a boat within 300 feet of a public beach, pier or authorized fishing groin, or fishing at any time in a bathing area, is prohibited. The lead-in limits it to persons 'in a park'.
entries.excerpt: No person in a park shall: ... (2) Fish off-shore from any type of boat within 300 feet of a public beach, pier, or authorized fishing groin or pier, nor shall any person at any time fish in any area where bathing is permitted. (Ord. No. 08-404, § 2, 8-21-2008)
entries.scope: Bradenton Beach city parks and adjoining water.
entries.note: Read 8 Oct 2026 through Municode's content service in the author's Chrome. Not drawn.

entries.title: Broward County: food fish in rivers, creeks, canals and inside waters by hook and line or cast net only
entries.effect: The 1921 act prohibits taking food fish from Broward's rivers, creeks, canals and inside waters by any means other than hook and line or a cast net up to 9 ft. Read literally, spearing in the Intracoastal and the county's canals is prohibited. Whether FWC has since repealed or superseded the act is not established, so treat it as live.
entries.excerpt: (a) It shall be unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corporation to take or catch any of the food fish from any of the rivers, creeks, canals and inside waters of Broward County, Florida, by or with any other means than a hook and line, or a common cast net, not to exceed a length of nine (9) feet, or a spread of eighteen (18) feet.
entries.scope: Broward County inside waters (undefined).

entries.title: Pinellas County parks and managed lands: fishing only in designated areas, none in bathing areas
entries.effect: On county-owned or managed lands, Fort De Soto, Sand Key and the other county parks included, fishing is prohibited except in public areas designated for it, and fishing from beaches in any bathing or swimming area is prohibited. How far the county's managed lands run into the water is not mapped.

entries.title: Proposed: shrimp fishery access area beside the Oculina Bank HAPC (not a spearfishing rule; comments to 14 Dec 2026)

entries.title: Hurricane port conditions: Coast Guard closes Florida ports to vessel traffic under Port Condition ZULU
entries.effect: When the Captain of the Port sets Port Condition ZULU before a storm, the Key West zone (§ 165.707) and the Sector Mobile zone, which covers the western Panhandle (§ 165.849), close to all vessel traffic except as authorized; in the Sector Miami zone (§ 165.706) all port waterfront operations are suspended. A dive boat leaving port during a storm closure is covered. These are not drawn: they apply to whole Coast Guard zones and only while a condition is set.

entries.title: Riviera Beach: no spearfishing by Phil Foster Park and the Blue Heron Bridge, or within 75 ft of any dock, wharf or bridge
entries.effect: Spearing (spear, gig or similar device used by a person submerged or partly under water) is banned in Lake Worth north of State Road 703 (Blue Heron Boulevard) and Phil Foster Memorial Park, within 1,000 ft west of the Singer Island shore and 1,000 ft north of SR 703; within 75 ft of any dock, wharf or bridge in the city; and within 150 ft of the southern shoreline of Phil Foster Memorial Park.
entries.excerpt: It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the activity of spear fishing, which includes the taking of any marine life through the instrumentality of a spear, gig or other similar device operated by a person submerged or partially underwater within the areas designated in subsections 13-31(2) and 13-31(3) and within 150 feet of the southern shoreline of Phil Foster Memorial Park. (Code 1957, § 16-16)
entries.scope: City of Riviera Beach: Lake Worth by Phil Foster Memorial Park and the Blue Heron Bridge, and every dock, wharf and bridge in the city.
entries.note: Read 11 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome through the Municode content service (api.municode.com/CodesContent, latest job), section text as returned, whitespace collapsed. The areas are those of § 13-31(a): "(2) That portion of the waters of Lake Worth bounded on the south by State Road No. 703 and Phil Foster Memorial Park; on the east by the shores of Singer Island; on the west by a line parallel to and 1,000 feet west of the shores of Singer Island; and, on the north by a line parallel to and 1,000 feet north of that portion of State Road No. 703 which lies between the western shore of Singer Island and the eastern shore of the mainland. (3) Within 75 feet of any dock, wharf or bridge." § 13-33 also bans swimming within 500 ft of the park north of SR 703. entries.effect: Spear fishing is banned within Palm Beach County park property. That reaches county beach parks, Phil Foster Park and Peanut Island.

entries.cite: City of Hollywood Code chs. 98, 99, 103, 131, 132 and 133, every section, checked 12 Nov 2026
entries.title: Hollywood: no spearfishing rule outside § 99.03(F) in the marine, beach, parks and offenses chapters (confirmed negative)
entries.effect: Besides the beach rule already drawn (§ 99.03(F), no spearfishing within 100 yd of the public beach and no loaded spear gun on the beach or in swimming areas), the only diving provision in these chapters is § 98.011(B), which requires a float and a diver-down flag for divers more than 150 ft from shore or in the Intracoastal. Neither the parks chapter nor the offenses chapters mention spears.
entries.excerpt: (B) Any person who engages in skin diving, scuba diving, or who performs or attempts to perform any form of underwater diving activities and more than 150 feet (50 yards) from the shore, in accordance with § 99.02(A), at low water or within the Intracoastal Waterway, within the city limits shall be equipped with a float and a State of Florida approved diver down.
entries.scope: City of Hollywood.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome on codelibrary.amlegal.com (code current through Ord. O-2026-12, passed 7-7-26): all 186 section pages of chs. 98 (Marine and Waterway Regulations), 99 (Municipal Beach), 103 (Parks and Recreation), 131 to 133 (offenses) fetched in page and searched for spear, scuba, snorkel, skin div and harpoon. The excerpt is § 98.011(B) as returned; the printed text ends at 'diver down'. Chapters outside these six were not section-searched: American Legal's chapter pages list sections without their text, and its search page returned nothing for a location filter. This closes the part of open question 25 that asked for Hollywood outside chapter 99, with that limit stated.

entries.title: Cocoa Beach: hook and line or hand-thrown cast net only in the listed residential canals (no spearing)
entries.effect: Taking fish by any means other than hook and line or a hand-thrown cast net is banned in the residential saltwater canals listed in (a)(1) to (12) and beyond, which cover the city's canal subdivisions on the Banana River side. Spearing is not among the allowed methods.
entries.excerpt: (a) Restricted areas. It shall be unlawful for any person to catch or take fish from the following salt water residential canals by means other than hook and line or cast net thrown by hand:
entries.full: (1) The canal lying between Willow Green Drive and Country Club Road bounded on the west by the exterior bulkhead line. (2) The canal located between Danube River Drive and Crystal River Drive. (3) Those canals bounded on the south by 4th Street South, bounded on the west by the interior bulkhead line, bounded on the north by Minutemen Causeway, and bounded by Brevard Avenue on the east. (4) Those canals lying within an area bounded on the south by Minutemen Causeway; bounded on the west by Crystal River Drive, and all other canals lying easterly of the interior bulkhead line; and bounded on the north by Andros Avenue and St. Croix Avenue. ... (6) The dredged major canal between the city's interior and exterior bulkhead lines, extending from the north end of Crystal River Drive northward to the west end of Andros Avenue. (7) The dredged major canal between the city's interior and exterior bulkhead lines, extending from the northwest corner of Yawl Drive residential land southward to the south city limits.
entries.scope: Listed residential canals in the City of Cocoa Beach.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome through api.municode.com search (client Cocoa Beach, product 13994) with a 4,000 character fragment, because the content service returned the node empty on 8 Oct 2026. The fragment ends partway through item (12), so the list after (12) and the history note were not read; the lead-in quoted as the excerpt is complete. Closes the Cocoa Beach part of open question 28. Not drawn: the canals are described by streets and bulkhead lines.

entries.title: Deerfield Beach: no swimming or diving into a marked No Entry Area off the city beaches
entries.effect: All persons, swimming, diving or wading, are barred from entering a marked No Entry Area. The section also sets a vessel exclusion zone about 400 ft east of mean high water along the city's beaches, shown on an Exhibit A held by the city clerk. No No Entry Area is located in the code text; they exist only where marked.
entries.excerpt: (4) "No Entry Area" - All vessels and all persons, either in vessels or swimming, diving or wading, are prohibited from entering the marked area.
entries.scope: Marked areas off the Deerfield Beach beaches.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome through the Municode content service. History: (Ord. No. 2018/004, § 2, 1-16-18). Closes the 30 Sep 2026 read owed on § 74-31. Not drawn: the marked areas are buoys on site and an exhibit, not a dataset; carried on the Deerfield Beach beach marker.

entries.title: Melbourne Beach: hook and line or hand-thrown cast net only in five named residential canals (no spearing)
entries.effect: Catching fish by any means other than hook and line, or any net other than a hand-thrown cast net, is banned in the five dredged residential canals named in the section (Driftwood Avenue, Riverview Lane, Sandy Key, Anchor Key and Pelican Key canals). Spearing is not an allowed method.
entries.excerpt: It shall be unlawful for any person to catch or take fish or attempt to catch or take fish by means other than hook and line or use any net other than a cast net thrown by hand in the following manmade saltwater residential canals:
entries.full: (1) The dredged canal lying between Driftwood Avenue on the north and Pelican Key, Riverview Lane, Sandy Key and other dredged canals on the south. (2) The dredged canal lying between Riverview Lane on the west and Sandy Key on the east. (3) The dredged canal lying between Sandy Key on the west and Anchor Key, Pelican Key and other dredged canals on the east. (4) The dredged canal lying between Pelican Key on the north and Anchor Key on the south. (5) The dredged canal lying between Anchor Key on the north and Riverview Lane on the south. ('75 Code, § 8-5) (Ord. 84-3, passed 5-8-84; Am. Ord. 85-1, passed 2-12-85)
entries.scope: Five named canals in the Town of Melbourne Beach.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome on codelibrary.amlegal.com (section page fetched in page, text extracted). Closes the Melbourne Beach part of open question 28. Not drawn: the canals are named by streets only.

entries.title: Pompano Beach: no spearfishing guns, gigs or slings on the beach or in the waters of the public beach; no scuba within 50 yd of shore
entries.effect: Using an underwater spearfishing gun, gig, sling, bow or similar gun on the beach or in the waters of the public beach is unlawful. Scuba diving within 50 yd east of the high tide line of all public beach areas is unlawful except when entering or leaving the water; snorkeling from the beach is allowed with a diver-down flag. How far 'the waters of the public beach' reach is not stated.
entries.excerpt: (M) Have or use surfboats or sailing devices or anything of a hard surface which can injure persons; use underwater spear-fishing guns, gigs, slings, bows or other type guns, excluding firearms which are subject to regulation under Chapter 790 F. S., on the beach or in the waters of the public beach. (N) Scuba diving within 50 yards eastward from the high tide line of all Public Beach areas, except when entering or leaving the water.
entries.full: Lead-in: "It shall be unlawful for any person to do any acts hereafter set out on the cultural or recreational facilities described in § 98.01 or on other public properties." (N) continues: "Snorkeling shall be permitted from the Public Beach. Divers must have an approved diver's down flag displayed in accordance with state requirements."
entries.scope: City of Pompano Beach public beach and its waters.
entries.note: Found 12 Nov 2026 by a statewide search of every Florida code on American Legal (codelibrary.amlegal.com search API with includeRegions fl), then read on the chapter page in the author's Chrome. History begins (Ord. 713, passed 7-28-59; ...). NEW: the 30 Sep 2026 sweep had only §§ 91.22 and 98.12 for Pompano Beach. Drawn as a marker on the beach (loc-pompano-beach); the state 100 yd beach buffer already covers the nearshore water.

entries.title: Mexico Beach: no diving from the city pier, and no swimming within 50 ft of it
entries.effect: No diving from the city pier and no swimming or otherwise occupying the water within 50 ft of it. The statewide 100 yd pier buffer already closes this water to spearfishing.
entries.excerpt: (1) It shall be unlawful for any person to dive from, launch boats from, or throw/push any articles, items or other paraphernalia, other than fishing tackle, from the pier. (2) It shall be unlawful for any person to swim, ride surfboards, operate boats of any kind, or otherwise occupy the waters within a 50-foot area of the pier.

entries.cite: Ocean Breeze, St. Lucie Village, Grant-Valkaria and Everglades City published codes, checked 12 Nov 2026
entries.title: Four small waterfront towns off Municode: no spearfishing or fishing rule found in what each town publishes (confirmed negative, with limits)
entries.effect: Ocean Breeze: the town's charter and related ordinances (54 pages, compiled 4 Oct 2023) contain no fishing, diving or water-use rule, and the legal description places the town line at the westerly shore of the Indian River. St. Lucie Village: the index of every ordinance and resolution from 1961 to 2022-4 lists none on fishing, spearfishing, diving or swimming; the closest are dock and seawall construction ordinances (91-5, 94-5) and a 1988 marina ordinance superseded in 1995. Grant-Valkaria: only the land development regulations are published online, and their single water section (§ 20-3668, Class II waters) is a 50 ft shoreline construction buffer, not a use rule. Everglades City: the city publishes only its land development code, charter, comprehensive plan and utility handbook, as image scans with no text layer; no general code of ordinances is online. County ordinances and the statewide rules apply in all four towns' waters.
entries.excerpt: [Method: Ocean Breeze 'Town Charter and Related Ordinances October 4 2023' PDF and St. Lucie Village 'Index of Ordinances & Resolutions (1961-Present)' PDF read with PDF.js in the author's Chrome and searched for fish, spear, dive, swim, dock, pier, boat, vessel, river, lagoon, marina and shore; Grant-Valkaria municipalcodeonline.com search for fishing (five hits, none a use rule); Everglades City public-documents page read and both linked PDFs found to be image-only.]
entries.scope: Towns of Ocean Breeze, St. Lucie Village and Grant-Valkaria; City of Everglades City.
entries.note: Closes the four 'not on Municode' towns left from neg-local-2026-11-11, except that Grant-Valkaria's and Everglades City's general codes are not published online, so a rule could exist in an uncodified or unpublished ordinance. Everglades City sits on the Barron River at the entrance to the Ten Thousand Islands and is the one of these four where that gap matters to divers; it is carried as an open question.

entries.cite: Canaveral Port Authority Tariff No. 16, Rule 380 (eff. 1 Oct 2026)
entries.title: Port Canaveral: underwater diving prohibited east of the Barge Canal lock through the jetties, unless the Harbormaster authorizes it
entries.effect: Underwater diving is prohibited in all water east of the Canaveral Barge Canal lock through the jetties to the Atlantic, except dive operations the Harbormaster authorizes. The rule is written for commercial dive operations, but its prohibition is not limited to them; the map reads it as closing the harbor to freediving and spearfishing too. It does not apply to waters under Navy, Army Corps or Coast Guard control.
entries.excerpt: Underwater diving operations are prohibited within the confines of Port Canaveral except when authorized by the Harbormaster. [...] For purposes of this Rule the confines of Port Canaveral are defined as including all water east of the Barge Canal Lock through the Jetties to the Atlantic Ocean. This Rule does not apply to waters under the control of the United States Navy, United States Army Corps of Engineers, or to the U.S. Coast Guard.
entries.scope: Port Canaveral harbor and the Canaveral Barge Canal east of the lock, to the jetties.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome from the tariff PDF on portcanaveral.com (page 14 to 15 of 52, Tariff No. 16 dated 1 Oct 2026); text taken from the PDF's own content streams. The omitted middle sentences set the notice, VHF and dive-flag duties for authorized operations. The Canaveral Port Authority is an independent special district; its tariff rules bind users of the port. The HTML tariff pages on the same site render empty. Jetty Park's posted rules page has no spearfishing or diving rule.

entries.cite: Port of Palm Beach District Tariff No. 24E, Item 546 (eff. 1 Oct 2025)
entries.title: Port of Palm Beach: underwater diving prohibited within the port unless the Director of Operations authorizes it
entries.effect: Underwater diving is prohibited within the confines of the Port of Palm Beach unless the Director of Operations authorizes it in writing at least 24 hours ahead, with certification and insurance. The tariff does not define 'the confines of the port'. Read conservatively, no freediving or spearfishing in the port's slips and turning basin.
entries.excerpt: 546 – DIVING OPERATIONS Underwater diving operations are prohibited within the confines of the Port of Palm Beach except when authorized by the Director of Operations. Written request must be made so that authorization can be granted no less than 24 hours in advance that includes a copy of the diver(s) certification(s) along with proof of commercial and dive accident insurance.
entries.scope: The Port of Palm Beach, Riviera Beach (Lake Worth Lagoon west of the inlet).
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome with PDF.js from the tariff PDF on portofpalmbeach.com (page 35). The Port of Palm Beach District is an independent special district. The fixed Coast Guard security zones of 33 C.F.R. § 165.760 also cover parts of the port.

entries.cite: Port Everglades Tariff No. 12, Item No. 280 (Broward County Administrative Code, eff. 1 Oct 2023, tariff of 1 Oct 2026)
entries.title: Port Everglades: no dive operations without the Harbormaster's prior written approval
entries.effect: Every dive operation inside Port Everglades needs the Harbormaster's prior written approval, requested by email at least 24 hours ahead, with VHF monitoring and hourly security calls. The item is written for vessel work; read conservatively, no freediving or spearfishing inside the port. A separate item limits the port's piers and docks to people with valid credentials and names fishing as an unauthorized activity there.
entries.excerpt: For all dive operations inside of Port Everglades, the following steps must be taken: [...] No dive operations are permitted without prior written approval from the Harbormaster.
entries.scope: Port Everglades (Broward County), inside the port.
entries.note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome with PDF.js from the complete Tariff No. 12 PDF linked from porteverglades.net/business/tariff (page 50). Port Everglades is a Broward County department; the tariff is part of the county's administrative code. The separate 'Section Two' PDF on the same page is an image scan.

entries.cite: JAXPORT, PortMiami and Port Tampa Bay tariffs in force 12 Nov 2026
entries.title: JAXPORT, PortMiami and Port Tampa Bay: no diving, swimming or fishing rule in the port tariff (confirmed negative)
entries.effect: The current tariffs of JAXPORT (1 Oct 2026), PortMiami (Terminal Tariff effective 1 Oct 2026) and Port Tampa Bay (2026 master tariff) contain no rule on diving, swimming, snorkeling, spearfishing or fishing. Coast Guard security zones and county and city ordinances still apply in those ports. Port Manatee's tariff is published only through a SharePoint and a Dropbox link and was not read; Port of Fernandina and Port Panama City were not checked.
